We have chosen this [view]

* *

[The interpretation of this verse is supported by the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿When the help of God and the victory come, and you see the people entering the religion of God in multitudes, then glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed He is ever Accepting of repentance﴾], as its soundness is confirmed: He, exalted is His remembrance, commanded him to glorify his Lord with His praise when the help of God and the conquest of Mecca came to him, and to seek His forgiveness, and informed him that He is Accepting of repentance toward whoever does that. In this there is a clear indication that His saying, exalted is His remembrance, ﴿that God may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what followed﴾, is only a report from God, exalted is His praise, to His Prophet, peace be upon him, about His recompense to him for his thankfulness for the blessing which He bestowed upon him, namely His granting him the conquest, because God, exalted is He, recompenses His servants for their deeds and not for anything else.

Moreover, the soundness of the report from him (ﷺ) that "he used to stand [in prayer] until his feet swelled. He was asked: 'O Messenger of God, do you do this when God has forgiven you what preceded of your sin and what followed?' He said: 'Should I not be a grateful servant?'" is a clear proof that what we have said on this matter is the correct view, and that God, blessed and exalted is He, promised His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) the forgiveness of his earlier sins, the conquest He granted him, and what came after it, in return for his thankfulness for the blessings He bestowed upon him.

Likewise he (ﷺ) used to say: "Indeed I seek forgiveness from God and turn to Him in repentance a hundred times every day." Had the meaning of this been that it is a report from God to His Prophet that He has forgiven him what preceded and what followed of his sin in a manner other than what we have mentioned, then His command to him to seek forgiveness after this verse would have no meaning, nor would the Prophet of God's seeking forgiveness from his Lord, majestic is His majesty, for his sins after it have any intelligible meaning; for seeking forgiveness means the servant asking his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to forgive his sins, and if there were no sins to be forgiven, then asking Him to forgive them would have no meaning, since it is absurd to say: "O God, forgive me a sin I did not commit."

It is mentioned that this surah was revealed to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on his return from Hudaybiyyah after the truce that took place between him and his people.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 48, verse 4:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿It is He who sent down tranquillity into the hearts of the believers, that they might increase in faith along with their faith. And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, and ever is Allah Knowing and Wise﴾ (48:4).

By His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, ﴿It is He who sent down tranquillity into the hearts of the believers﴾, He means: Allah sent down calm and tranquillity into the hearts of those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, toward faith and the truth with which Allah sent you, O Muhammad. The disagreement of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) concerning the meaning of tranquillity (sakinah) has already been mentioned earlier, and the correct view on that, with the sufficient proofs, need not be repeated in this place.

﴿That they might increase in faith along with their faith﴾ means: that they might increase, through their affirmation of the obligations which Allah has newly prescribed for them, which had not been binding upon them, ﴿in faith along with their faith﴾, meaning: that they might increase, beyond their faith, in the obligations that had been binding upon them before that.

The people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿It is He who sent down tranquillity into the hearts of the believers﴾, he said: Tranquillity is mercy. ﴿That they might increase in faith along with their faith﴾, he said: Allah, may His praise be exalted, sent His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) with the testimony that there is no god but Allah. When they affirmed it, He added prayer for them; when they affirmed it, He added fasting for them; when they affirmed it, He added zakat for them; when they affirmed it, He added the Hajj for them; then He perfected their religion, saying ﴿This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favour upon you﴾. Ibn Abbas said: So the most firm, most truthful and most complete faith of the people of the earth and the people of the heavens is the testimony that there is no god but Allah.

As for His saying ﴿And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth﴾

His saying, may He be exalted, means: To Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, helpers through whom He takes vengeance upon whomever He wills of His enemies. ﴿And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise﴾ means: Allah, may He be exalted, has never ceased to have knowledge of what is to occur before it occurs, and of what His creatures will do, Wise in His management.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 48, verse 5:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein eternally, and remove from them their misdeeds. And that is, in the sight of Allah, a great achievement.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Indeed We have granted you a clear victory, so that you may give thanks to your Lord and praise Him for that, and so that He may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what followed. And that the believers in Allah may praise their Lord and give thanks to Him for His bounty upon them, by what He has bestowed upon them of the victory which He granted and decreed between them and their enemies from among the polytheists, by making them prevail over them. Thereby He admits them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding in them without end; and that He may remove from them the evil of their deeds through the good deeds they perform, in gratitude to their Lord for what He has decreed for them and bestowed upon them. ﴿And that is, in the sight of Allah, a great achievement.﴾ He, the Exalted, says: That which Allah promised them of this reward, namely their admission to gardens beneath which rivers flow, and the removal of their misdeeds through the good of their deeds, which they perform, is with Allah for them, ﴿a great achievement﴾. He says: a triumph on their part in what they had hoped for and strove for, and a salvation from what they had feared of the punishment of Allah, a great one. The narration has already been mentioned that this verse was revealed when the believers said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), or when he recited to them the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed We have granted you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what followed﴾. "This is for you, O Messenger of Allah; so what is for us?" Thus Allah made clear to them what He would do with them.

⁕ Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ ... to His words ﴿and remove from them their misdeeds﴾: Allah, glorified is He, informed His Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him).

* *

Regarding His words ﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women﴾:

The lam in His words ﴿that He may forgive you what preceded of your sin﴾ is connected, by way of repeating the sentence, to ﴿Indeed We have granted you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you﴾, meaning: Indeed We have granted you victory, that He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow. For this reason the conjunction waw, which enters speech for coordination, did not enter here, so it does not say: "and that He may admit the believing men."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 48, verse 6–7:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And that He may punish the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and the polytheist women, who assume about Allah an assumption of evil. Upon them is a circle of evil; and Allah has been angry with them and has cursed them and prepared for them Hell, and evil is it as a destination﴾ [48:6]; and ﴿To Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, and ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise﴾ [48:7].

He, may He be remembered, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Indeed We have given you a clear victory, so that Allah may forgive you, and admit the believing men and believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow, and that He may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, by Allah's granting you victory, O Muhammad, that which He granted you of support over the polytheists of Quraysh, so that they are humiliated and grieved by it, and their hope is frustrated, the hope they had cherished of seeing weakness, feebleness, and turning away from you among the people of faith in the immediate life of this world, and the burning of the Fire and abiding therein in the deferred life of the Hereafter. ﴿And the polytheist men and the polytheist women﴾ means: and He likewise punishes the polytheist men and the polytheist women. ﴿Who assume about Allah﴾ that He will not support you, and the people of faith in you, against your enemies, and that He will not make manifest His word, making it superior to the word of the disbelievers in Him. That assumption of evil was among their suppositions which Allah mentioned in this passage. He, may He be remembered, says: upon the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women who assumed this assumption, is a circle of evil, meaning a circle of punishment revolving around them through it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 48, verses 8–9:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner (8) That you may believe in Allah and His Messenger and support him and honour him and exalt Him morning and evening (9)﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying: to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, We have sent you﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿as a witness﴾ over your community regarding how they responded to you concerning what I called them to, of the message with which I sent you to them, ﴿and a bringer of good tidings﴾ to them of Paradise if they answer you to the upright religion to which I called them, ﴿and a warner﴾ to them of the punishment of Allah if they turn away from what you brought them from your Lord.

Then the reciters differed over the recitation of His saying ﴿That you may believe in Allah and His Messenger and support him and honour him and exalt Him﴾. The majority of the reciters of the regions read all of it with the (taʾ, second person plural), except Abu Jaʿfar al-Madani and Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAla, ﴿That you (tuʾminū) ... and you (tuʿazzirūhu) ... and you (tuwaqqirūhu) ... and you (tusabbihūhu)﴾, meaning: that you, O people, may believe in Allah and His Messenger. Abu Jaʿfar and Abu ʿAmr read all of it with the (yāʾ, third person plural), ﴿That they (yuʾminū) ... and they (yuʿazzirūhu) ... and they (yuwaqqirūhu) ... and they (yusabbihūhu)﴾, meaning: We have sent you as a witness to the creation, so that they may believe in Allah and His Messenger and support him.

The correct view on this matter is to say: these are two well-known recitations, both sound in meaning, so whichever one the reciter reads is correct.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾: he says, a witness over his community that he has conveyed to them, and a bringer of good tidings of Paradise for whoever obeys Allah, and a warner of the Fire.

* *

And His saying ﴿and support him and honour him﴾

The people of interpretation differed concerning its meaning. Some of them said: glorify him and revere him.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿and support him﴾: meaning, to magnify him; ﴿and honour him﴾: meaning, to exalt him.

- I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿and support him and honour him﴾: all of this is exaltation and magnification.

Others said: the meaning of ﴿and support him﴾ is: and help him, and the meaning of ﴿and honour him﴾ is: and glorify him.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and support him﴾: help him; ﴿and honour him﴾: Allah commanded that he be made master and glorified.

- Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿and support him﴾, he said: help him, and ﴿honour him﴾: that is, exalt him.

- Abu Hurayrah al-Duba'i narrated to me, saying: Harami narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Abu Bishr Jaʿfar ibn Abi Wahshiyyah, from ʿIkrimah: ﴿and support him﴾, he said: they fight alongside him with the sword.

- Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to me, from Abu Bishr, from ʿIkrimah, the same.

- Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me, saying: ʿUthman ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, from Saʿid, from Abu Bishr, from ʿIkrimah, similar.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya and Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, both saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from ʿIkrimah, the same.

Others said: the meaning of that is: and magnify him.

Mention of those who said that:

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and support him and honour him﴾: it is obedience to Allah.

These statements are close in meaning, even though their wording differs. The meaning of ta'zir (support) in this place is strengthening with help and aid, and this is only achieved through obedience, exaltation and reverence.

We have already explained the meaning of this, with its evidence, earlier, in what suffices so as not to repeat it here.

As for tawqir, it means exaltation, reverence and magnification.

He says: and pray to Him, meaning to Allah, in the mornings and evenings.

The pronoun in His saying ﴿and exalt Him﴾ refers to Allah alone, not to the Messenger. It has been mentioned that in some readings it is: ﴿and exalt Allah morning and evening﴾.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and exalt Him morning and evening﴾; in some readings: ﴿and exalt Allah morning and evening﴾.

- Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, regarding some letters: ﴿and exalt Allah morning and evening﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 48, verse 10:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, [O Muhammad], they are actually pledging allegiance to Allah. The hand of Allah is over their hands. So whoever breaks his word only breaks it to the detriment of himself, and whoever fulfills what he has promised Allah—He will give him a great reward.﴾ (48:10)

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you﴾ at al-Hudaybiyah from among your companions, on condition that they not flee when meeting the enemy and not turn their backs to them. ﴿they are actually pledging allegiance to Allah﴾ meaning: by their pledge to you they are pledging to Allah, because Allah guaranteed them Paradise in return for their fulfilling that to Him.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you﴾, he said: It was on the day of al-Hudaybiyah.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, they are actually pledging allegiance to Allah. The hand of Allah is over their hands. So whoever breaks his word only breaks it to the detriment of himself﴾: They are those who pledged allegiance on the day of al-Hudaybiyah.

Regarding His saying ﴿The hand of Allah is over their hands﴾ there are two interpretations: First, the hand of Allah is over their hands at the time of the pledge, because they were pledging allegiance to Allah through their pledge to His Prophet (ﷺ). The second: the power of Allah is over their power in supporting His Messenger (ﷺ), because they only pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for his support against the enemy.

* *

And His saying ﴿So whoever breaks his word only breaks it to the detriment of himself﴾

He, the Exalted, says: So whoever breaks his pledge to you, O Muhammad, and violates it, not supporting you against your enemies, and opposes what he promised his Lord, ﴿only breaks it to the detriment of himself﴾, meaning: he only breaks his pledge, because by that action he removes himself from those whom Allah promised Paradise for fulfilling the pledge. So by his breaking he harms no one but himself, and he breaks only against himself. As for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah, blessed and exalted, is his helper against his enemies, whether the breaker among them breaks his word or fulfills his pledge.

* *

And His saying ﴿And whoever fulfills what he has promised Allah﴾

... the verse. He, the Exalted, says: And whoever fulfills what he has pledged to Allah of steadfastness when meeting the enemy in the way of Allah and supporting His Prophet (ﷺ) against his enemies, ﴿He will give him a great reward﴾, meaning: Allah will give him a great reward, namely that He will admit him to Paradise as recompense for his fulfilling what he pledged to Allah, and bound himself to His Messenger, to remain steadfast with him in time of hardship, by solemn oaths.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿He will give him a great reward﴾: It is Paradise.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 48, verse 11:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿The desert Arabs who stayed behind will say to you, "Our properties and our families kept us busy, so ask forgiveness for us." They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Say, "Who then has any power at all against God, if He intends harm for you or intends benefit for you? Rather, God is ever Acquainted with what you do."﴾

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "They will say to you, O Muhammad, those whom God left behind with their families, away from accompanying you and going out with you on your journey, and your march that you marched to Mecca as a pilgrim performing the minor pilgrimage (ʿumrah), visiting the Sacred House of God, when you returned to them and rebuked them for staying behind from you: 'Our properties kept us busy, the tending of our wealth and the setting right of our livelihoods and our families, so ask forgiveness for us from our Lord for our staying behind from you.'" God, whose praise is great, said, refuting them in what they said: "These desert Arabs who stayed behind from you say with their tongues what is not in their hearts." That is their asking the Messenger of God ﷺ to seek forgiveness for them, meaning: they ask him without repentance from them and without regret for what preceded of their disobedience to God in staying behind from accompanying the Messenger of God ﷺ and marching with him. ﴿Say, "Who then has any power at all against God"﴾: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet: "Say to these desert Arabs who ask you to seek forgiveness for them because they stayed behind from you: If I should seek forgiveness for you, O people, and then God intends your destruction or the destruction of your properties and families, or intends benefit for you by increasing your wealth and setting right your families, then who is it that is able to repel what God intends for you of good or evil? God cannot be overpowered by anyone, and no conqueror can overcome Him."

* *

As for His words ﴿Rather, God is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾:

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The matter is not as these hypocrites among the desert Arabs suppose, that God does not know what they conceal of hypocrisy. Rather, God has never ceased to be Acquainted with what they do of good and evil. Nothing of the deeds of His creation is hidden from Him, whether secret or public, and He counts them against them until He recompenses them for them. It is reported that when the Messenger of God ﷺ intended to march to Mecca in the year of Hudaybiyyah as a pilgrim performing the minor pilgrimage, he summoned the Arabs and those around his city from the people of the deserts and the desert Arabs to go out with him, fearing that his people, the Quraysh, would confront him with war or would block him from the House. He himself ﷺ entered the state of ihram for the minor pilgrimage and took the sacrificial animals with him, so that people would know that he did not desire war. Many of the desert Arabs held back from him and stayed behind contrary to him. They are the ones whom God, blessed and exalted, meant by His words ﴿The desert Arabs who stayed behind will say to you, "Our properties and our families kept us busy"﴾ ... the verse.

Scholars of the biography (sīrah) and military campaigns (maghāzī) of the Messenger of God ﷺ said what we have said on this matter, among them Ibn Ishaq.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us from Ibn Ishaq with this. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿The desert Arabs who stayed behind will say to you, "Our properties and our families kept us busy"﴾, he said: "The Arabs of Medina: Juhaynah and Muzaynah. He summoned them to accompany him to Mecca. They said: 'We will go with him to a people who have come to him and killed his companions, and we will fight them!' So they made excuses with preoccupation."

The readers differed in reading His words ﴿if He intends harm for you﴾. The readers of Medina and Basra and some readers of Kufa recited it ﴿darran﴾ with a fatha on the dad, meaning harm, which is the opposite of benefit. The majority of the Kufan readers recited it ﴿durran﴾ with a damma on the dad, meaning misery and sickness.

The reading I prefer of the two is the fatha on the dad in this place, given His words ﴿or intends benefit for you﴾, for it is well known that the opposite of benefit is harm (ḍarr), although the other reading is also sound in meaning.

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Nay, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families again, and that was made appealing in your hearts, and you harboured an evil assumption, and you were a people doomed to ruin.﴾ (12)

Exalted is He, says, addressing these Bedouin who made excuses to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ upon his return from his journey, with their words ﴿Our property and our families kept us busy﴾: You did not stay behind out of opposition to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he set out away from you, and you sat back from accompanying him because of your preoccupation with your property and families. Rather, you stayed behind in your dwellings after him, thinking that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and those with him among his Companions would be destroyed, and so would never return to you, through the enemy annihilating them. ﴿And that was made appealing in your hearts﴾: Satan made that appealing in your hearts and made it seem correct to you, until staying behind from him seemed good to you, so you sat back from accompanying him. ﴿And you harboured an evil assumption﴾: he says, you thought that Allah would not give victory to Muhammad ﷺ and his believing Companions over their enemies, and that the enemy would overpower and defeat them and kill them.

And those versed in interpretation said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿Those who were left behind of the Bedouin will say to you...﴾ down to His words ﴿and you were a people doomed to ruin﴾, he said: They thought about the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and his Companions that they would not return from that direction, and that they would be destroyed, and that is what kept them behind from the Prophet of Allah ﷺ.

* *

And as for His words ﴿and you were a people doomed to ruin﴾:

He says: and you were a people who were lost, fit for nothing good. It has been said that "bur" in the dialect of Adhri'at means corrupt; as for the Arabs, it means "nothing." From this is the saying of Abu al-Darda': "So what they gathered became bur," meaning gone, having become void, with nothing left of it. From this is also the verse of Hassan ibn Thabit:

"Height does not benefit the foolish of hearts,
and God does not guide the path of the ruined people [al-bur]."

[The verse is by Hassan ibn Thabit, satirising a people whose tall bodies bring no good so long as they are foolish (nawk, i.e. stupidity). "Bur" means lost ones. In Lisan al-Arab (root b-w-r) it says: a man is bur, and likewise two people, plural and feminine. In the revelation: "and you were a people doomed to ruin." It says: "bur" here may be the plural of ba'ir, like hawl and ha'il. Al-Akhfash related from some that it is a dialect form and not a plural of ba'ir, as one says "anta bashar" and "antum bashar." He said: al-Farra' said regarding His words "and you were a people doomed to ruin": "bur" is a verbal noun that may be singular or plural. In Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 305), from Ibn Abbas, he said: "bur" in the dialect of the Azd of Oman means corrupt; "and you were a people doomed to ruin": people who were corrupt. And "bur" in Arabic speech means "nothing." It is said: their deeds became bur, and their dwellings qubur (graves).]

And those versed in interpretation said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿and you were a people doomed to ruin﴾, he said: corrupt.
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿and you were a people doomed to ruin﴾, he said: "bur" is that in which there is no good at all.
- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿and you were a people doomed to ruin﴾, he said: destroyed.

The interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger – then indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a blaze﴾ [48:13] and ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [48:14].

His Exalted remembrance says to these hypocrites among the Bedouins: "And whoever of you, O Bedouins, and of others, does not believe in Allah and His Messenger, by affirming him in what he reported and acknowledging what he brought of the truth from his Lord – then indeed, We have prepared for them all a blaze of Fire, which will flare up against them in Hell when they arrive there on the Day of Resurrection."

It is said regarding this: "sa'artu al-nar" (I kindled the fire), when I ignite it, so "a sa'iruha sa'aran" (I kindle it). It is also said: "sa'artuha" when I stir it. The kindling-tool (mis'ar) is so named because the fire is stirred with it, and from this the saying: "innahu la-mis'ar harb" (he is indeed a kindler of war), meaning its igniter and agitator.

* *

As for His words, ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾:

His Exalted remembrance says: "To Allah belongs the sovereignty of the heavens and the earth, so none of you, O hypocrites, can repel from Him what He intends for you of punishment for your hypocrisy if you persist in it, or prevent Him from pardoning you if He pardons, if you repent of your hypocrisy and disbelief." This is an exhortation from Allah, majestic is His praise, to these Bedouins who lagged behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to repent and return to the command of Allah by obeying His Messenger ﷺ. He says to them: "Hasten to repentance for your lagging behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, for Allah forgives those who repent." ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ means: Allah has never ceased to be one who pardons the punishment of those of His servants who turn back to Him from their sins and disobediences, and Merciful toward them, not to punish them for their sins after they have repented of them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 48, verse 15:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who were left behind will say, when you set out to take spoils, "Leave us that we may follow you." They wish to change the words of Allah. Say, "You will not follow us; thus has Allah said before." So they will say, "Rather, you envy us." Rather, they did not understand except a little.﴾ (15)

Exalted is His remembrance says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Those who were left behind will say, O Muhammad, regarding their families, about accompanying you, when you set out as a pilgrim (mu'tamir) intending the Sacred House of Allah, when you and those who accompany you set out on that journey toward the spoils which Allah has bestowed upon you and them." ﴿To take them﴾: that refers to what Allah had promised the people of al-Hudaybiyah of the spoils of Khaybar. ﴿Leave us that we may follow you﴾ to Khaybar, that we may witness with you the fighting against its people. ﴿They wish to change the words of Allah﴾: he says, they wish to alter the promise of Allah which He made to the people of al-Hudaybiyah. That is because Allah made the spoils of Khaybar theirs, and promised them that in exchange for the spoils of the people of Makkah, when they turned away from them under a treaty and did not gain anything from them.

Those of the exegetes said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from Makkah, and Allah promised him many spoils, so Khaybar was hastened for him. The ones left behind said, ﴿Leave us that we may follow you. They wish to change the words of Allah﴾, and they are the spoils that He, mighty is His praise, mentioned: ﴿when you set out to take spoils﴾, and He presented to them the fighting against a people of great might.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from a man of his companions, from Muqsim, who said: When Allah promised them that He would open Khaybar for them, and Allah had promised it to those who witnessed al-Hudaybiyah, and He gave nothing of it to anyone other than them, when the hypocrites learned that it was the spoil, they said, ﴿Leave us that we may follow you. They wish to change the words of Allah﴾. He says: what He promised them.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Those who were left behind will say, when you set out﴾ ... the verse, and they are those who stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at al-Hudaybiyah. It was mentioned to us that when the polytheists prevented the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at al-Hudaybiyah from the Sacred Mosque and the offering, al-Miqdad said: "O Prophet of Allah, by Allah, we will not say as the chiefs of the Children of Israel said to their prophet, ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are sitting here﴾, but we will say: Go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed we are fighting alongside you both." When the companions of the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) heard that, they pledged allegiance upon what he had said. When the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) saw that, he made peace with Quraysh and returned that same year.

Others said: Rather, by His saying ﴿They wish to change the words of Allah﴾ He meant their desire to go out with the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) on his campaign, and Allah, blessed and exalted, has said, ﴿Say: You will never go out with me, and you will never fight an enemy with me.﴾

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Those who were left behind will say, when you set out to take spoils, "Leave us that we may follow you"﴾ ... the verse, Allah, mighty and majestic, said when he returned from his campaign, ﴿So they asked your permission to go out. Say: You will never go out with me, and you will never fight an enemy with me﴾ ... the verse. "They wish to change the words of Allah": they wished to alter the words of Allah which He said to His Prophet (ﷺ), and go out with him, and Allah and His Prophet (ﷺ) refused that for them.

What Ibn Zayd said has no basis, because the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic, ﴿So they asked your permission to go out. Say: You will never go out with me, and you will never fight an enemy with me﴾ was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) only upon his return from Tabuk, and it was meant for those who stayed behind from him when he set out for Tabuk to fight the Romans. There is no disagreement among the scholars of the campaigns of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that Tabuk was after the conquest of Khaybar and also after the conquest of Makkah. How, then, could it be permissible that the matter as we have described it be what is meant by Allah's saying ﴿They wish to change the words of Allah﴾, when it is a report about those who stayed behind from going with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he set out as a pilgrim intending the House, and the polytheists prevented him from the House? Those who stayed behind at the campaign of Tabuk, and the campaign of Tabuk had not yet taken place on the day this verse was revealed, nor had His saying ﴿So they asked your permission to go out. Say: You will never go out with me, and you will never fight an enemy with me﴾ been revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Since that is so, the correct view on this is what Mujahid and Qatadah said, as we have explained.

The readers differed in the recitation of His saying ﴿They wish to change the words of Allah﴾. The majority of the readers of Madinah and Basrah, and some of the readers of Kufah, recited ﴿kalam Allah﴾ as a verbal noun (masdar) with the alif. The majority of the readers of Kufah recited ﴿kalim Allah﴾ without the alif, meaning the plural of "kalimah" (word). According to us, these are two widely transmitted readings in the recitation of the cities, close in meaning; whichever of the two a reader recites is correct, though I lean more toward the recitation with the alif.

* *

And His saying ﴿Say: You will not follow us; thus has Allah said before﴾

Exalted is His remembrance says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Say to these who were left behind from going with you, O Muhammad: You will not follow us to Khaybar if we wish to set out against them to fight them." ﴿Thus has Allah said before﴾: he says, thus Allah said to us before our return to you, that the spoils of Khaybar belong to those who witnessed al-Hudaybiyah with us, and you are not among those who witnessed it; so you have no right to follow us to Khaybar, because its spoils are for others.

Those of the exegetes said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿thus has Allah said before﴾, meaning: the spoils were only made for the people of jihad, and the spoils of Khaybar were for those who witnessed al-Hudaybiyah, and there was no share in them for anyone else.

* *

And His saying ﴿So they will say, "Rather, you envy us."﴾

That you will give them a share of the spoils with you if we witness with you; therefore you prevent us from going out with you.

Those of the exegetes said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿So they will say, "Rather, you envy us."﴾ That you will give them a share of the spoils with you.

* *

And His saying ﴿Rather, they did not understand except a little.﴾

Exalted is His remembrance says to His Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions: The matter is not as these hypocrite Bedouins say, that you only prevent them from following you out of envy of them, lest they obtain spoils from the enemy along with you. Rather, they did not understand from Allah what is for them and against them of the matter of religion except a little, a small amount; and had they understood, they would not have said to the Messenger of Allah and the believers in him, when they had informed them of what Allah, exalted is His remembrance, had said, that He had forbidden them the spoils of Khaybar, that you only prevent us from accompanying you there because you envy us.

The Interpretation of His, the Exalted, words: ﴿Say to the desert Arabs who stayed behind: "You will be called to a people of great military might; you will fight them, or they will submit. So if you obey, Allah will give you a good reward, but if you turn away as you turned away before, He will punish you with a painful punishment."﴾ (48:16)

God, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿to the desert Arabs who stayed behind﴾ from marching with you, ﴿"You will be called to﴾ fight ﴿a people of great military might﴾ in battle, ﴿great﴾.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning those whom God, the Mighty and Majestic, described as the people to whom these desert Arabs who stayed behind would be called to fight. Some of them said: They are the people of Persia.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Abi Najih, from Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿of great military might﴾ — the people of Persia.

- Isma'il ibn Musa al-Fazari related to us, saying: Dawud ibn al-Zabarqan informed us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, regarding His words ﴿You will be called to a people of great military might﴾, he said: Persia and the Byzantines (al-Rum).

He said: Dawud informed us, from Sa'id, from al-Hasan, the same.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan said, regarding His words ﴿You will be called to a people of great military might﴾: They are Persia and the Byzantines.

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿of great military might﴾: They are Persia.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿You will be called to a people of great military might﴾, he said: al-Hasan said: They were called to Persia and the Byzantines.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿You will be called to a people of great military might﴾: Persia and the Byzantines.

Others said: They are Hawazin at Hunayn.

Those who said this:

- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Abu Bishr informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿You will be called to a people of great military might﴾, he said: Hawazin.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ikrimah, regarding this verse ﴿You will be called to a people of great military might﴾, he said: Hawazin and Thaqif.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿of great military might, you will fight them or they will submit﴾, he said: They are Hawazin and Ghatafan on the day of Hunayn.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Say to the desert Arabs who stayed behind: You will be called to a people of great military might﴾. So on the day of Hunayn they were called to Hawazin and Thaqif, and some of them responded well and were eager for jihad.

Others said: Rather, they are Banu Hanifah.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri: ﴿of great military might﴾, he said: Banu Hanifah with Musaylimah the Liar.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Hushaym, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ikrimah, that they used to add to it Hawazin and Banu Hanifah.

Others said: This verse has not yet come to pass.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Hurayrah: ﴿You will be called to a people of great military might﴾ — this verse has not yet come.

Others said: They are the Byzantines (al-Rum).

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Awf related to me, saying: Abu al-Mughirah related to us, saying: Safwan ibn Amr related to us, saying: al-Faraj ibn Muhammad al-Kala'i related to us, from Ka'b, who said: ﴿of great military might﴾: the Byzantines.

The most correct of these views, in our judgment, is to say: God, the Exalted, informed us that these desert Arabs who stayed behind would be called to fight a people of great military might in battle and of valor in wars. Neither report nor reason has established for us that the intended people are Hawazin, nor Banu Hanifah, nor Persia, nor the Byzantines, nor any specific individuals among them. It is permissible that some of these groups are meant, and permissible that others are meant. The most correct statement regarding it is to say as God, His praise be mentioned, said: they will be called to a people of great military might.

* *

As for His words ﴿you will fight them or they will submit﴾:

God, the Exalted, says to the desert Arabs who stayed behind: You will fight those whom you are called to fight, or they will submit without war or fighting.

It has been mentioned that in some readings it is recited ﴿you will fight them or they will submit﴾ [with the verb in the subjunctive, يسلموا]. According to this reading, although it differs from the codices of the major cities and from what the readers of proof (al-qurra' al-hujjah) follow, and in my view it is not permissible to recite it so, its interpretation would be: you will fight them continually until they submit, or until they submit.

* *

As for His words ﴿So if you obey, Allah will give you a good reward﴾:

God, the Exalted, says: So if you obey God by answering Him when He calls you to fight these people of great military might, and you respond to fighting them and to jihad alongside the believers, ﴿Allah will give you a good reward﴾, meaning: God will give you, for your answering Him in fighting them, Paradise, which is the good reward. ﴿But if you turn away as you turned away before﴾, meaning: If you disobey your Lord, turn your backs on His obedience and oppose His command, leaving off fighting the people of great military might when you are called to fight them, ﴿as you turned away before﴾, meaning: as you disobeyed Him in His command to you to march with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to Mecca, before you were called to fight the people of great military might, ﴿He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾, meaning: a grievous one, which is the punishment of the Fire, for your disobedience to Him and your abandoning of jihad and fighting alongside the believers.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 48, verse 17:

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor is there blame upon the lame, nor is there blame upon the sick﴾ and so on, ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow; and whoever turns away, He will punish him with a painful punishment﴾ (17).

He, the Exalted, says: There is no narrowness (ḍayq) upon the blind among you, O people, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick, in staying behind from jihad with the believers and in not attending the fighting alongside them when they meet their enemy, because of the impairments that are in them and the causes that prevent them from attending it.

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor is there blame upon the lame, nor is there blame upon the sick﴾: He said: All of this concerns jihad.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: Then Allah excused those among the people who have excuses, saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor is there blame upon the lame, nor is there blame upon the sick﴾.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor is there blame upon the lame, nor is there blame upon the sick﴾: He said: It concerns jihad in the way of Allah.

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿There is no blame upon the blind﴾ ... the verse, meaning in fighting.

* *

And His words ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾

He, the Exalted, says: And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, by responding to the fight against the enemies of Allah from among the polytheists, and to fighting alongside the believers seeking the Face of Allah when called to that, Allah will admit him on the Day of Resurrection to gardens beneath which rivers flow. ﴿And whoever turns away﴾ means: whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, staying behind from fighting the polytheists when called to it, and does not respond to the call of Allah and His Messenger, He will punish him with a painful punishment, and that is the punishment of Hell on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 48, verse 18–19:

The interpretation of the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you, [O Muhammad], under the tree. He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquillity upon them and rewarded them with an imminent conquest﴾ [48:18] ﴿and much war booty which they will take. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise﴾ [48:19].

He, the Exalted, says: Indeed Allah was pleased, O Muhammad, with the believers ﴿when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree﴾, meaning the pledge of the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Hudaybiyah, when they pledged to him to fight the Quraysh and not to flee, and not to turn their backs to them, under the tree. Their pledge to him there was, as has been reported, under a tree.

The cause of this pledge, as has been said, was that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had sent Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) with his message to the chiefs of Quraysh, and Uthman was somewhat slow to return, so it was thought that he had been killed, and he called his companions to renew the pledge to fight them as I have described. They pledged to him on that. This is the pledge called the Pledge of Pleasure (bay'at al-Ridwan). Those who gave this pledge, as reported in the saying of some of them, were one thousand four hundred; in the saying of some of them, one thousand five hundred; and in the saying of some of them, one thousand three hundred.

Mention of the narration concerning the cause of this pledge as we have described:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: some of the people of knowledge told me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned Khirash ibn Umayyah al-Khuza'i and sent him to the Quraysh in Makkah, and mounted him on his camel called al-Tha'lab, to convey to their nobles what he had come with, and that was when he descended at al-Hudaybiyah. They hamstrung the camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and wanted to kill him, but the Ahabish prevented him, and they let him go, until he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

⁕ He said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Someone I do not doubt related to me, from Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned Umar ibn al-Khattab to send him to Makkah, to convey to the nobles of Quraysh what he had come with. He said: O Messenger of Allah, I fear Quraysh for myself, and there is no one from the Banu Adi ibn Ka'b in Makkah who would protect me, and Quraysh knows my enmity towards them and my harshness against them. But I will direct you to a man who is more honoured there than I am: Uthman ibn Affan." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned Uthman and sent him to Abu Sufyan and the nobles of Quraysh to inform them that he had not come for war, but had come only as a visitor to this House, magnifying its sanctity. Uthman went out towards Makkah, and Aban ibn Sa'id ibn al-As met him when he entered Makkah, or before he entered it, and dismounted from his mount, carried him before himself, then seated him behind him and gave him protection until he conveyed the message of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Uthman went until he came to Abu Sufyan and the chiefs of Quraysh, and conveyed to them what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had sent him with. When Uthman finished the message of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they said to him: If you wish to circumambulate the House, then circumambulate it. He said: I would not do so until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ circumambulates it. So Quraysh held him back with them, and word reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims that Uthman had been killed."

⁕ He said: Salamah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr related to me: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was informed that Uthman had been killed, he said: We will not depart until we fight these people. He called the people to the pledge, and it was the Pledge of Pleasure under the tree. The people used to say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ pledged them to death. Jabir ibn Abd Allah used to say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not pledge us to death, but he pledged us that we would not flee. The people pledged to the Messenger of Allah, and none of the Muslims who attended it stayed behind except al-Jadd ibn Qays, brother of the Banu Salamah. Jabir ibn Abd Allah used to say: It is as if I see him clinging to the armpit of his she-camel, having hidden behind it, concealing himself from the people." Then he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [and it is said] that what was mentioned about Uthman was false."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Ammarah al-Asadi related to us, he said: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, he said: Musa ibn Ubaydah informed us, from Iyas ibn Salamah, who said: Salamah said: "While we were resting at midday during the time of al-Hudaybiyah, the caller of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called out: O people, the pledge, the pledge! The Holy Spirit (may the blessings of Allah be upon him) has descended. He said: So we rushed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while he was under a sumurah tree, and we pledged to him. That is the saying of Allah: ﴿Indeed, Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree﴾."

Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan al-Yashkuri related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Yazid related to us, from Isma'il, from Amir, who said: The first to pledge the Pledge of Pleasure was a man from the Banu Asad called Abu Sinan ibn Wahb.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Hammad related to us, he said: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: My grandfather, called Hazn, was among those who pledged under the tree. We came to it the following year, and it had been concealed from us.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Hammad related to us, he said: Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, that it reached him that the people pledged to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to death, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ﴿According to your ability﴾. The tree under which they pledged was in a valley towards Makkah. They claimed that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) passed by that place after the tree had gone, and said: Where was it? Some of them began saying: Here, and some said: Here. When their disagreement increased, he said: Leave off this pretension. The tree was gone; it was a sumurah tree, either a flood took it away or something else did.

Mention of the number of those who gave this pledge:

We have mentioned the disagreement of those who differed about their number, and we will mention the reports from those who spoke these sayings, if Allah the Exalted wills.

Mention of those who said: their number was one thousand four hundred:

⁕ Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi related to me, he said: My father related to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: "On the day of al-Hudaybiyah we were one thousand four hundred. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took our pledge that we would not flee, and he did not take our pledge to death. He said: We all pledged except al-Jadd ibn Qays, who hid under the armpit of his she-camel."

⁕ Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: Al-Qasim ibn Abd Allah ibn Amr informed me, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah: "They were on the day of al-Hudaybiyah fourteen hundred. We pledged to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while Umar held his hand under the tree, which was a sumurah tree, and we all pledged except al-Jadd ibn Qays al-Ansari, who hid under the armpit of his camel. Jabir said: We pledged to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that we would not flee, and we did not pledge him to death."

⁕ Yusuf ibn Musa al-Qattan related to us, he said: Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik and Sa'id ibn Sharahil al-Misri related to us, the two of them said: Layth ibn Sa'd al-Misri related to us, he said: Abu al-Zubayr related to us, from Jabir, who said: "On the day of al-Hudaybiyah we were one thousand four hundred. We pledged to him while Umar held his hand under the tree, which was a sumurah tree, and we pledged to him that we would not flee, and we did not pledge him to death," meaning the Prophet ﷺ.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, the two of them said: Ibn Abi Adi related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, that it was said to him: "Jabir ibn Abd Allah says that the companions of the tree were one thousand five hundred." Sa'id said: Jabir forgot; he himself said to me they were one thousand four hundred.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: We, the companions of al-Hudaybiyah, were one thousand four hundred.

Mention of those who said: their number was one thousand five hundred and twenty-five:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to us, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿Indeed, Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree﴾, he said: The people of the pledge under the tree were one thousand five hundred and twenty-five.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 48, verse 18–19:

The interpretation of the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you, [O Muhammad], under the tree. He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquillity upon them and rewarded them with an imminent conquest﴾ [48:18] ﴿and much war booty which they will take. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise﴾ [48:19].

He, the Exalted, says: Indeed Allah was pleased, O Muhammad, with the believers ﴿when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree﴾, meaning the pledge of the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Hudaybiyah, when they pledged to him to fight the Quraysh and not to flee, and not to turn their backs to them, under the tree. Their pledge to him there was, as has been reported, under a tree.

The cause of this pledge, as has been said, was that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had sent Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) with his message to the chiefs of Quraysh, and Uthman was somewhat slow to return, so it was thought that he had been killed, and he called his companions to renew the pledge to fight them as I have described. They pledged to him on that. This is the pledge called the Pledge of Pleasure (bay'at al-Ridwan). Those who gave this pledge, as reported in the saying of some of them, were one thousand four hundred; in the saying of some of them, one thousand five hundred; and in the saying of some of them, one thousand three hundred.

Mention of the narration concerning the cause of this pledge as we have described:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: some of the people of knowledge told me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned Khirash ibn Umayyah al-Khuza'i and sent him to the Quraysh in Makkah, and mounted him on his camel called al-Tha'lab, to convey to their nobles what he had come with, and that was when he descended at al-Hudaybiyah. They hamstrung the camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and wanted to kill him, but the Ahabish prevented him, and they let him go, until he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

⁕ He said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Someone I do not doubt related to me, from Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned Umar ibn al-Khattab to send him to Makkah, to convey to the nobles of Quraysh what he had come with. He said: O Messenger of Allah, I fear Quraysh for myself, and there is no one from the Banu Adi ibn Ka'b in Makkah who would protect me, and Quraysh knows my enmity towards them and my harshness against them. But I will direct you to a man who is more honoured there than I am: Uthman ibn Affan." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned Uthman and sent him to Abu Sufyan and the nobles of Quraysh to inform them that he had not come for war, but had come only as a visitor to this House, magnifying its sanctity. Uthman went out towards Makkah, and Aban ibn Sa'id ibn al-As met him when he entered Makkah, or before he entered it, and dismounted from his mount, carried him before himself, then seated him behind him and gave him protection until he conveyed the message of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Uthman went until he came to Abu Sufyan and the chiefs of Quraysh, and conveyed to them what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had sent him with. When Uthman finished the message of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they said to him: If you wish to circumambulate the House, then circumambulate it. He said: I would not do so until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ circumambulates it. So Quraysh held him back with them, and word reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims that Uthman had been killed."

⁕ He said: Salamah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr related to me: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was informed that Uthman had been killed, he said: We will not depart until we fight these people. He called the people to the pledge, and it was the Pledge of Pleasure under the tree. The people used to say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ pledged them to death. Jabir ibn Abd Allah used to say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not pledge us to death, but he pledged us that we would not flee. The people pledged to the Messenger of Allah, and none of the Muslims who attended it stayed behind except al-Jadd ibn Qays, brother of the Banu Salamah. Jabir ibn Abd Allah used to say: It is as if I see him clinging to the armpit of his she-camel, having hidden behind it, concealing himself from the people." Then he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [and it is said] that what was mentioned about Uthman was false."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Ammarah al-Asadi related to us, he said: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, he said: Musa ibn Ubaydah informed us, from Iyas ibn Salamah, who said: Salamah said: "While we were resting at midday during the time of al-Hudaybiyah, the caller of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called out: O people, the pledge, the pledge! The Holy Spirit (may the blessings of Allah be upon him) has descended. He said: So we rushed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while he was under a sumurah tree, and we pledged to him. That is the saying of Allah: ﴿Indeed, Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree﴾."

Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan al-Yashkuri related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Yazid related to us, from Isma'il, from Amir, who said: The first to pledge the Pledge of Pleasure was a man from the Banu Asad called Abu Sinan ibn Wahb.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Hammad related to us, he said: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: My grandfather, called Hazn, was among those who pledged under the tree. We came to it the following year, and it had been concealed from us.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Hammad related to us, he said: Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, that it reached him that the people pledged to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to death, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ﴿According to your ability﴾. The tree under which they pledged was in a valley towards Makkah. They claimed that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) passed by that place after the tree had gone, and said: Where was it? Some of them began saying: Here, and some said: Here. When their disagreement increased, he said: Leave off this pretension. The tree was gone; it was a sumurah tree, either a flood took it away or something else did.

Mention of the number of those who gave this pledge:

We have mentioned the disagreement of those who differed about their number, and we will mention the reports from those who spoke these sayings, if Allah the Exalted wills.

Mention of those who said: their number was one thousand four hundred:

⁕ Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi related to me, he said: My father related to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: "On the day of al-Hudaybiyah we were one thousand four hundred. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took our pledge that we would not flee, and he did not take our pledge to death. He said: We all pledged except al-Jadd ibn Qays, who hid under the armpit of his she-camel."

⁕ Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: Al-Qasim ibn Abd Allah ibn Amr informed me, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah: "They were on the day of al-Hudaybiyah fourteen hundred. We pledged to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while Umar held his hand under the tree, which was a sumurah tree, and we all pledged except al-Jadd ibn Qays al-Ansari, who hid under the armpit of his camel. Jabir said: We pledged to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that we would not flee, and we did not pledge him to death."

⁕ Yusuf ibn Musa al-Qattan related to us, he said: Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik and Sa'id ibn Sharahil al-Misri related to us, the two of them said: Layth ibn Sa'd al-Misri related to us, he said: Abu al-Zubayr related to us, from Jabir, who said: "On the day of al-Hudaybiyah we were one thousand four hundred. We pledged to him while Umar held his hand under the tree, which was a sumurah tree, and we pledged to him that we would not flee, and we did not pledge him to death," meaning the Prophet ﷺ.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, the two of them said: Ibn Abi Adi related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, that it was said to him: "Jabir ibn Abd Allah says that the companions of the tree were one thousand five hundred." Sa'id said: Jabir forgot; he himself said to me they were one thousand four hundred.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: We, the companions of al-Hudaybiyah, were one thousand four hundred.

⁕ Bishr related to me, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: "Those who pledged to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ under the tree, for whom the spoils of Khaybar were made, were on that day one thousand five hundred, and they pledged that they would not flee from him."
