Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 48, verse 20–21:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Allah has promised you much booty that you will take, and He has hastened this for you and restrained the hands of the people from you, that it may be a sign for the believers and that He may guide you to a straight path.﴾ (48:20) ﴿And [He has promised] another [victory] not yet within your capability, but Allah has encompassed it, and ever is Allah over all things competent.﴾ (48:21)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the people of the Pledge of Good Pleasure (bay'at al-Ridwan): ﴿Allah has promised you, O people,﴾ ﴿much booty that you will take﴾.

The exegetes differed concerning these spoils that Allah mentioned He had promised these people: which spoils are they? Some of them said: they are every spoil which Allah granted the believers in Him from the wealth of the people of polytheism, from the time this verse was revealed upon the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Allah has promised you much booty that you will take﴾: He said: "The much booty they were promised is what they take until today."

On this interpretation, the speech may allow that the second spoils are intended to be the first spoils, and its meaning would then be: "He rewarded them with a near victory and much booty they will take; Allah promised you, O people, these spoils that you will take, and you are reaching them as a promise; so He made for you the near victory, from the conquest of Khaybar." It may also be that the second is other than the first, with the first being the spoils of Khaybar, and the second spoils that He promised them being the spoils of the rest of the people of polytheism apart from them.

Others said: these spoils that Allah promised these people are the spoils of Khaybar.

Those who said this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Allah has promised you much booty that you will take﴾: "It is the day of Khaybar." He said: "My father used to say this."

* *

As for His words ﴿and He has hastened this for you﴾:

The exegetes differed concerning what was hastened for them. A group said: the spoils of Khaybar, and what is postponed is all the conquests of the Muslims after that time until the Hour.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and He has hastened this for you﴾: He said: "He hastened Khaybar for you."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿and He has hastened this for you﴾, and it is Khaybar.

Others said: rather, He meant by that the truce that was between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Quraysh.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and He has hastened this for you﴾: He said: "The truce."

The most correct of these interpretations, in my view, is what Mujahid said, namely that what Allah rewarded them with from their march that year, together with the near victory, is the much booty from the spoils of Khaybar. This is because the Muslims had not taken any spoil after Hudaybiyyah, and they had not achieved a conquest nearer to their pledge to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Hudaybiyyah than the conquest of Khaybar and its spoils.

As for His words ﴿Allah has promised you much booty﴾, it refers to all the spoils that Allah granted them after Khaybar, such as the spoils of Hawazin, Ghatafan, Persia and Rome.

We have said this in this manner rather than the spoils of Khaybar, because Allah informed that He hastened for them this [spoil] which He rewarded them from their march which they made with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Makkah, and for what He knew of the soundness of their intention in fighting its people, when they pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that they would not flee from him. There is no doubt that what was hastened for them is other than what was not hastened for them.

* *

As for His words ﴿and restrained the hands of the people from you﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the people of the Pledge of Good Pleasure: and Allah restrained the hands of the polytheists from you.

Then the exegetes differed concerning those whose hands were restrained from them, who they were. Some of them said: they are the Jews; Allah restrained their hands from the families of those who marched from Medina with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Makkah.

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿and restrained the hands of the people from you﴾: from their homes and from their families in Medina when they marched to Hudaybiyyah and to Khaybar, and Khaybar was in that direction.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿and restrained the hands of the people from you﴾: He said: "He restrained the hands of the people from their families in Medina."

Others said: rather, by that is meant the hands of the Quraysh, when Allah held them back from them, so they were not able to do them any harm.

What Qatada said in this matter is, in my view, more resembling the interpretation of the verse, because Allah's restraining of the hands of the polytheists of Makkah from the people of Hudaybiyyah was mentioned by Allah after this verse, in His words ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah﴾. Thereby it is known that the restraint which Allah mentioned in His words ﴿and restrained the hands of the people from you﴾ is other than the restraint which Allah mentioned after this verse in His words ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah﴾.

* *

As for His words ﴿and that it may be a sign for the believers﴾:

He says: and that His restraint of their hands from their families be a sign and a lesson for the believers in Him, so that they know that Allah is the One who takes charge of their protection and safeguarding in their presence and their absence, and that they fear Allah regarding themselves, their wealth and their families, by guarding and by good guardianship, as long as they remain in obedience to Him, adhering to His command and prohibition.

The exegetes said in agreement with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿and that it may be a sign for the believers﴾: He says: that is a sign for the believers, the restraint of the hands of the people from their families. ﴿and that He may guide you to a straight path﴾: He says: and that He may direct you, O believers, to a clear path with no crookedness in it, making it clear to you, which is that you trust in your Lord in all your affairs, and rely upon Him in all of them, so that He may protect you with His protection of you in your selves, families and wealth on your march to Makkah with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. You have indeed seen the effect of Allah's action toward you when you trusted in this march of yours.

* *

As for His words ﴿And [He has promised] another [victory] not yet within your capability, but Allah has encompassed it﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: and your Lord promised you, O people, the conquest of another town that you have not been able to conquer, which Allah has encompassed for you, until He conquers it for you.

The exegetes differed concerning this other town and other village which He promised them the conquest of, and which He informed them He encompasses. Some of them said: it is the land of Persia and Rome, and whatever the Muslims conquer of the lands until the Hour.

Those who said this:

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Simak al-Hanafi, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: ﴿And another [victory] not yet within your capability﴾: Persia and Rome.

He said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Ibn Abi Layla that he said regarding this verse: ﴿And another [victory] not yet within your capability﴾: "Persia and Rome."

Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Zayd ibn Hubab narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, the like of it.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And another [victory] not yet within your capability, but Allah has encompassed it﴾: He said: it was narrated from al-Hasan, who said: "It is Persia and Rome."

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And another [victory] not yet within your capability﴾: "They had not conquered it until today."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from al-Hakam, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, regarding His words ﴿And another [victory] not yet within your capability﴾: He said: "Persia and Rome."

Others said: rather, it is Khaybar.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And another [victory] not yet within your capability﴾ ... the verse, he said: "It is Khaybar."

I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿And another [victory] not yet within your capability, but Allah has encompassed it﴾: "He means Khaybar, which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent them to that day, saying: Do not mutilate, do not steal from the spoils, and do not kill a child."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿And another [victory] not yet within your capability, but Allah has encompassed it﴾: "It is Khaybar. They did not mention it or hope for it until Allah informed them of it."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿And another [victory] not yet within your capability﴾: meaning the people of Khaybar.

Others said: rather, it is Makkah.

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿And another [victory] not yet within your capability, but Allah has encompassed it﴾: "We used to narrate that it is Makkah."

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿And another [victory] not yet within your capability﴾: He said: "It has reached us that it is Makkah."

The view which Qatada stated resembles more what the apparent wording of the revelation indicates, because Allah informed those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ under the tree that He encompasses a town they were not able to conquer. And it is understood that one does not say of people that they were unable to conquer a city unless they had attempted it and it was made impossible for them; but as for those who had not attempted it, it is not said that they were unable to conquer it.

Given that this is so, and it being known that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had not intended Khaybar for war before the revelation of this verse, nor had he directed toward it an army or a detachment to fight its people, it is established that what is meant by His words ﴿And another [victory] not yet within your capability﴾ is other than it, and that it is the one he had dealt with and attempted, and it was made impossible, so it was Makkah and its people. Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, informed His Prophet ﷺ and the believers that He encompasses it and its people, and that He grants them its conquest, and Allah is over all things that He wills powerful, nothing He wills being impossible for Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 48, verse 20–21:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Allah has promised you much booty that you will take, and He has hastened this for you and restrained the hands of the people from you, that it may be a sign for the believers and that He may guide you to a straight path.﴾ (48:20) ﴿And [He has promised] another [victory] not yet within your capability, but Allah has encompassed it, and ever is Allah over all things competent.﴾ (48:21)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the people of the Pledge of Good Pleasure (bay'at al-Ridwan): ﴿Allah has promised you, O people,﴾ ﴿much booty that you will take﴾.

The exegetes differed concerning these spoils that Allah mentioned He had promised these people: which spoils are they? Some of them said: they are every spoil which Allah granted the believers in Him from the wealth of the people of polytheism, from the time this verse was revealed upon the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Allah has promised you much booty that you will take﴾: He said: "The much booty they were promised is what they take until today."

On this interpretation, the speech may allow that the second spoils are intended to be the first spoils, and its meaning would then be: "He rewarded them with a near victory and much booty they will take; Allah promised you, O people, these spoils that you will take, and you are reaching them as a promise; so He made for you the near victory, from the conquest of Khaybar." It may also be that the second is other than the first, with the first being the spoils of Khaybar, and the second spoils that He promised them being the spoils of the rest of the people of polytheism apart from them.

Others said: these spoils that Allah promised these people are the spoils of Khaybar.

Those who said this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Allah has promised you much booty that you will take﴾: "It is the day of Khaybar." He said: "My father used to say this."

* *

As for His words ﴿and He has hastened this for you﴾:

The exegetes differed concerning what was hastened for them. A group said: the spoils of Khaybar, and what is postponed is all the conquests of the Muslims after that time until the Hour.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and He has hastened this for you﴾: He said: "He hastened Khaybar for you."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿and He has hastened this for you﴾, and it is Khaybar.

Others said: rather, He meant by that the truce that was between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Quraysh.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿and He has hastened this for you﴾: He said: "The truce."

The most correct of these interpretations, in my view, is what Mujahid said, namely that what Allah rewarded them with from their march that year, together with the near victory, is the much booty from the spoils of Khaybar. This is because the Muslims had not taken any spoil after Hudaybiyyah, and they had not achieved a conquest nearer to their pledge to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Hudaybiyyah than the conquest of Khaybar and its spoils.

As for His words ﴿Allah has promised you much booty﴾, it refers to all the spoils that Allah granted them after Khaybar, such as the spoils of Hawazin, Ghatafan, Persia and Rome.

We have said this in this manner rather than the spoils of Khaybar, because Allah informed that He hastened for them this [spoil] which He rewarded them from their march which they made with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Makkah, and for what He knew of the soundness of their intention in fighting its people, when they pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that they would not flee from him. There is no doubt that what was hastened for them is other than what was not hastened for them.

* *

As for His words ﴿and restrained the hands of the people from you﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the people of the Pledge of Good Pleasure: and Allah restrained the hands of the polytheists from you.

Then the exegetes differed concerning those whose hands were restrained from them, who they were. Some of them said: they are the Jews; Allah restrained their hands from the families of those who marched from Medina with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Makkah.

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿and restrained the hands of the people from you﴾: from their homes and from their families in Medina when they marched to Hudaybiyyah and to Khaybar, and Khaybar was in that direction.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿and restrained the hands of the people from you﴾: He said: "He restrained the hands of the people from their families in Medina."

Others said: rather, by that is meant the hands of the Quraysh, when Allah held them back from them, so they were not able to do them any harm.

What Qatada said in this matter is, in my view, more resembling the interpretation of the verse, because Allah's restraining of the hands of the polytheists of Makkah from the people of Hudaybiyyah was mentioned by Allah after this verse, in His words ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah﴾. Thereby it is known that the restraint which Allah mentioned in His words ﴿and restrained the hands of the people from you﴾ is other than the restraint which Allah mentioned after this verse in His words ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah﴾.

* *

As for His words ﴿and that it may be a sign for the believers﴾:

He says: and that His restraint of their hands from their families be a sign and a lesson for the believers in Him, so that they know that Allah is the One who takes charge of their protection and safeguarding in their presence and their absence, and that they fear Allah regarding themselves, their wealth and their families, by guarding and by good guardianship, as long as they remain in obedience to Him, adhering to His command and prohibition.

The exegetes said in agreement with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿and that it may be a sign for the believers﴾: He says: that is a sign for the believers, the restraint of the hands of the people from their families. ﴿and that He may guide you to a straight path﴾: He says: and that He may direct you, O believers, to a clear path with no crookedness in it, making it clear to you, which is that you trust in your Lord in all your affairs, and rely upon Him in all of them, so that He may protect you with His protection of you in your selves, families and wealth on your march to Makkah with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. You have indeed seen the effect of Allah's action toward you when you trusted in this march of yours.

* *

Those of the interpreters of the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Allah said ﴿then they would not find any protector or helper﴾ — one who would help them against Allah.

* *

As for His words ﴿That is the way of Allah which has already passed among those who preceded﴾:

Allah, mentioned and exalted, says: If these disbelievers of Quraysh had fought you, Allah would have forsaken them, so that He would defeat them before you, by forsaking them as He forsook their like among the people of disbelief in Him, who fought His allies among the nations that passed before them. He put ﴿the way of Allah﴾ in the accusative case without repeating its wording, because in His words ﴿they would have turned their backs; then they would not find any protector or helper﴾ there is the meaning "I have prescribed defeat and forsaking for them." Therefore it was said ﴿the way of Allah﴾ as a verbal noun (maṣdar) derived from the meaning of the speech rather than from its wording. It is also permissible that it be an explanation of what came before it in the speech.

The Exegesis of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the heart of Makkah after He had made you victorious over them. And ever is Allah, of what you do, Seeing.﴾

Allah, the Exalted, says to His Messenger ﷺ, concerning those who pledged allegiance in the Pledge of Ridwan: ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you﴾, meaning: Allah restrained the hands of the polytheists who had come out against the army of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Hudaybiyah, seeking to catch them off guard so as to inflict harm upon them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then sent out and they were brought to him as captives, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ released them and granted them pardon, and did not kill them. So Allah said to the believers: And it is He who restrained the hands of these polytheists from you, and your hands from them in the heart of Makkah, after He had made you victorious over them.

Traditions have come in agreement with what we have said concerning this.

Mention of the narrations to that effect:

* Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, saying: I heard my father say: al-Husayn ibn Waqid informed us, saying: Thabit al-Bunani related to me, from ʿAbdullah ibn Mughaffal, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting at the base of a tree at al-Hudaybiyah, and a branch from the tree was over his back, so I lifted it off his back. ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) was before him, and Suhayl ibn ʿAmr, who was the representative of the polytheists. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to ʿAli: Write: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Suhayl held his hand back and said: We do not recognize "the Most Merciful." Write in our agreement what we recognize. The Messenger of Allah said: Write: In Your name, O Allah. So he wrote it. He said: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed upon with the people of Makkah. Suhayl again held his hand back and said: We would have wronged you if you were a messenger. Write in our agreement what we recognize. He said: Write: This is what Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib has agreed upon, and I am the Messenger of Allah. Then thirty young men armed with weapons came out to us and rushed at our faces, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked against them, and Allah blinded their sight, so we rose against them and seized them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: Did you come out under the protection of anyone? He said: So he released them. He said: Then Allah revealed: ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the heart of Makkah after He had made you victorious over them﴾.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Thabit, from ʿAbdullah ibn Mughaffal, who said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ at al-Hudaybiyah, beneath the tree which Allah mentioned in the Qur'an, and a branch of that tree was over the back of the Prophet ﷺ, so I lifted it from his back. Then he mentioned a narration similar to the hadith of Muhammad ibn ʿAli, from his father.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: One whom I do not accuse of falsehood related to me, from ʿIkrimah, the freed slave of Ibn ʿAbbas, that the Quraysh had sent forty or fifty men of theirs and ordered them to circle the army of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in order to strike one of his companions. They were seized and brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he pardoned them and let them go. They had been pelting the army of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with stones and arrows. Ibn Humayd said: Salamah said: Ibn Ishaq said: Concerning that Allah said: ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them﴾ … the verse.

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: The Prophet of Allah came forth performing ʿumrah, and his companions seized some people of the sacred precinct who were heedless, so the Prophet ﷺ released them. That is the "making victorious" in the heart of Makkah.

* Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to us, saying: ʿUbaydullah ibn ʿAishah narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, that eighty men of the people of Makkah descended upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions from the mountain of al-Tanim at the time of the dawn prayer, intending to kill them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ seized them and set them free, so Allah revealed: ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them﴾ … to the end of the verse.

Qatadah used to say concerning this:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning his words: ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them﴾ … the verse. He said: "The heart of Makkah" is al-Hudaybiyah. [[There may be a lacuna here. In Ibn Kathir, from Qatadah: "It was mentioned to us that a man called Ibn Zunaym looked down upon the pass..." etc.]] A man called Rahm looked down upon the pass from al-Hudaybiyah, and the polytheists shot him with an arrow and killed him. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ then sent horsemen, and they brought him twelve horsemen from among the disbelievers. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said to them: Do you have a covenant with me? Do you have a pledge of protection from me? They said: No. So he released them, and Allah revealed in that regard the Qur'an: ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them﴾ … to His words ﴿of what you do, Seeing﴾.

Others said concerning this:

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yaʿqub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Jaʿfar, from Ibn Abza, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ set out with the sacrificial animals and reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, ʿUmar said to him: O Prophet of Allah, you will enter upon a people who are at war with you without weapons or mounts. So he sent to Madinah and did not leave any mount or weapon there except that he took it. When he approached Makkah, they prevented him from entering, so he travelled until he came to Mina and alighted there. His spy came to him to say that ʿIkrimah ibn Abi Jahl had come out against us with five hundred men. He said to Khalid ibn al-Walid: O Khalid, this is your cousin, who has come upon you with horsemen. Khalid said: I am the Sword of Allah and the Sword of His Messenger. That day he was named "Sword of Allah." He said: O Messenger of Allah, send me wherever you wish. So he dispatched him with horsemen, and he encountered ʿIkrimah in the ravine and defeated him until he drove him into the orchards of Makkah. Then he returned a second time and defeated him until he drove him into the orchards of Makkah, then returned a third time until he drove him into the orchards of Makkah. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them﴾ … to His words ﴿a painful punishment﴾. He said: So Allah restrained the Prophet from them after having made him victorious over them, because of remnants of the Muslims who had remained among them, lest the horses trample them without knowledge.

* * *

And His words: ﴿And ever is Allah, of what you do, Seeing﴾.

Allah, the Exalted, says: And Allah is Seeing of your deeds and their deeds; nothing of them is hidden from Him.

**Commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque, and [barred] the offering (hadi) from reaching its place of sacrifice. And had there not been believing men and believing women whom you did not know, [and] you might have trampled them, and thus guilt would have befallen you on their account without knowledge, [that] Allah might admit into His mercy whom He wills. Had they been distinguished, We would surely have punished those among them who disbelieved with a painful punishment.﴾ (48:25)**

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: These polytheists of Quraysh are the ones who denied the Oneness of Allah. They barred you, O believers in Allah, from entering the Sacred Mosque, and they barred the offering (hadi) from reaching its place of sacrifice, detained (ma'kufan), meaning held back from reaching its place of sacrifice.

The position of *an* (أن) in the phrase ﴿أَنْ يَبْلُغَ﴾ is in the accusative case, since it is governed either by *ma'kufan* (معكوفا) or by *sadda* (صدّوا), whichever you prefer. One of the grammarians of Basra used to say about this: "They barred the offering, detained, out of dislike that it should reach its place of sacrifice."

By Allah's words ﴿أَنْ يَبْلُغَ مَحِلَّهُ﴾ (that it should reach its place of sacrifice), He means that it should reach its place of slaughter (mahall nahrihi), which is the entry into the Sanctuary (haram), and the place where, once it arrives, its slaughter becomes lawful. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had brought with him, when he set out for Mecca on that journey, seventy camels (badana) for sacrifice.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salama narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhri, from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Miswar ibn Makhrama and Marwan ibn al-Hakam, that both of them narrated to him, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out in the year of Hudaybiyya intending to visit the House, not intending fighting, and he brought with him seventy camels for sacrifice, and the people were seven hundred men, so each camel was for ten [persons].

And with words similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of His words ﴿They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque, and [barred] the offering, detained from reaching its place of sacrifice﴾, the people of ta'wil (interpretation) said:

Those who said that:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque, and [barred] the offering, detained﴾: meaning held back ﴿from reaching its place of sacrifice﴾. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions came as pilgrims (mu'tamirin) in Dhu al-Qa'da, with the offering with them, until when they reached Hudaybiyya, the polytheists barred them. So the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) made a treaty with them that he would return in that year, and then return in the following year, and stay in Mecca for three nights, and not enter it except with the weapons of the rider (sealed weapons carried in sheaths), and not take out anyone of its people. So they slaughtered the offering, shaved their heads, and trimmed their hair. Then, when the following year came, the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions came and entered Mecca as pilgrims in Dhu al-Qa'da, and he stayed there three nights. The polytheists had acted treacherously toward him when they turned him back, so Allah exacted retribution from them, and admitted him into Mecca in that same month in which they had turned him back. Then Allah revealed: ﴿The sacred month for the sacred month, and sacred things are [subject to] retribution﴾ (2:194).

⁕ Muhammad ibn Ammara al-Asadi and Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to me, the wording being that of Ibn Ammara, they said: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, he said: Musa ibn Ubayda informed us, from Iyas ibn Salama ibn al-Akwa', from his father, who said: Quraysh sent Suhayl ibn Amr, Huwaytib ibn Abd al-Uzza, and Hafs ibn Fulan to the Prophet (ﷺ) to make peace with him. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw them, and among them was Suhayl ibn Amr, he said: "Allah has made your affair easy. These people are coming to you with their kin, and asking you for peace. So send forth the offering, and make the talbiya (the call of pilgrimage) audible, perhaps that will soften their hearts." So they made the talbiya from the sides of the camp until their voices rose with the talbiya. Then they came and asked him for peace. He said: While the people were making a truce, and among the Muslims there were some polytheists, it was said that Abu Sufyan was [among them]. He said: The valley was flowing with men. He said: Iyas said, Salama said: I brought six polytheists, fully armed, driving them before me, who had no power over themselves for benefit or harm. I brought them to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he did not strip them nor kill them, and he pardoned them. He said: Then we attacked those among the polytheists who had some of ours in their hands, and we did not leave a single man of ours in their hands except that we rescued him. He said: And we overcame those of theirs who were in our hands. Then Quraysh sent Suhayl ibn Amr and Huwaytib, and they took over the matter of their peace, and the Prophet (ﷺ) sent Ali to write the treaty. So Ali wrote between them: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), has agreed upon with Quraysh: they have made peace with him that there shall be no secret raiding (ihlal) nor theft (imtilal), and that whoever comes to Mecca from the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), as a pilgrim or as one performing umra, or seeking some bounty of Allah, he is safe in his blood and property; and whoever comes to Medina from Quraysh, passing through toward Egypt or toward Syria seeking some bounty of Allah, he is safe in his blood and property; and that whoever comes to Muhammad (ﷺ) from Quraysh, he shall be returned to them, and whoever comes to them from the companions of Muhammad, he shall be theirs." This weighed heavily upon the Muslims, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever comes to them from us, may Allah banish him, and whoever comes to us from them, we will return him to them, and Allah knows the Islam within his self, and will make for him a way out." They made peace with him on the condition that he would perform umra the following year in this month, that no one would enter upon us with horses or weapons, except what the traveler carries in his sheath, that he would stay among us for three nights, and that this offering, wherever we detain it, will reach its place of sacrifice, and that it will not be brought forward against us. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "We drive it, and you turn back its faces." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out with the offering, and the people set out.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Ammara narrated to me, he said: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, he said: Musa informed us, he said: Abu Murra, the mawla of Umm Hani', informed me, from Ibn Umar, who said: "The offering was beneath the mountains that overlook the valley of al-Thaniyya when the polytheists confronted it and turned back its faces. He said: So the Prophet (ﷺ) slaughtered the offering when they detained it, at Hudaybiyya, and he shaved his head, and some people followed his example when they saw him shave, while others hesitated, saying: 'Perhaps we will circumambulate the House.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'May Allah have mercy on those who shave.' It was said: 'And those who trim?' He said: 'May Allah have mercy on those who shave.' It was said: 'And those who trim?' He said: 'And those who trim.'"

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated to us, he said: Umar ibn Dharr al-Hamdani narrated to us, from Mujahid, "that the Prophet (ﷺ) performed three umras, all of them in Dhu al-Qa'da, returning after each of them to Medina. Among them was the umra in which the offering was barred, and he slaughtered it in its place, near the tree. They stipulated with him that he would come the following year as a pilgrim, and enter Mecca, and circumambulate the House for three days, then leave, and that they would not detain anyone who came with him, nor take out from Mecca anyone of the Muslims who had been in it before his arrival. When the following year came, he entered Mecca and stayed there three days, circumambulating the House. When it was the third day, near noon, they sent to him: 'Your people are harmed by your staying.' So it was proclaimed among the people: 'The sun shall not set while any of the Muslims who came with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remain.'"

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Miswar ibn Makhrama, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) went out at the time of Hudaybiyya with some fifteen hundred of his companions, until when they reached Dhu al-Hulayfa, he garlanded the offering (qallada al-hadi) and marked it (ashaarahu), and he put on the state of ihram for umra, and sent ahead of him a spy of his from Khuza'a to inform him about Quraysh. The Prophet (ﷺ) proceeded until, when he reached the pool of al-Ashtat near Qu'ayqi'an, his Khuza'i spy came to him and said: "I left Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy and Amir ibn Lu'ayy, who have gathered the Ahabish for you, and have assembled for you great armies, and they are going to fight you and bar you from the House." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Advise me. Do you think we should turn upon the children of those who helped them, and strike them? If they sit, they will sit wounded and grieved; and if they persist, it will be a neck that Allah cuts off? Or do you think that we should intend the House, and whoever bars us from it, we fight him?" Then Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have not come to fight anyone, but whoever stands between us and the House, we will fight him." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Then set off." Abu Hurayra used to say: "I never saw anyone who consulted his companions more than the Prophet (ﷺ)." So they set off until, when they were in part of the way, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Khalid ibn al-Walid is at al-Ghamim with a cavalry of Quraysh as a vanguard, so take the path to the right." By Allah, Khalid did not perceive them until he suddenly found himself at the dust of the army, and he set off galloping to warn Quraysh. The Prophet (ﷺ) proceeded until, when he was at the ascent (al-thaniyya) by which they would descend upon them, his she-camel knelt with him. The people said: "Hal, hal!" [Hal hal: a command to camels to drive them on.] He said: "What is 'hal'?" They said: "Al-Qaswa' has balked." [Khalaʾat al-naqa takhla': she stopped moving. Khalaʾ among camels is like hiran among horses (Lisan al-Arab: kh-l-a).] The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "She has not balked, nor is that her habit, but the One who restrained the elephant has restrained her." Then he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, they will not ask me for any arrangement by which they glorify the sacred things of Allah except that I will give it to them." Then she was urged on, and she sprang up and turned away from them until she stopped at the farthest part of Hudaybiyya, at a small well with little water, which people were barely drawing from, so the people soon drained it. The thirst was complained of to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he drew an arrow from his quiver and commanded them to put it into the well. By Allah, it continued to gush forth water for them until they departed from it. While they were in that state, Budayl ibn Warqa' al-Khuza'i came with a group of Khuza'a, who were among the people of Tihama the trusted advisers (a'yba nasih) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "I left Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy and Amir ibn Lu'ayy, who have settled at the outskirts of the waters of Hudaybiyya, with them the nursing she-camels with their young, and they are going to fight you and bar you from the House." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "We have not come to fight anyone, but we have come as pilgrims. Quraysh has been worn down by war and harmed by it. If they wish, we will make a truce with them for a period, and they will leave the way clear between me and the people. If I prevail, they may enter what the people have entered, if they wish; otherwise they will have rested. But if they refuse, by Him in whose hand is my soul, I will certainly fight them over this matter of mine until my neck is severed, or Allah will surely carry out His command." Budayl said: "We will convey to them what you say." So he set off until he came to Quraysh and said: "We have come to you from this man, and we heard him say a statement. If you wish, we will present it to you." Their foolish ones said: "We have no need for you to tell us anything of him." But those of judgment among them said: "Tell us what you heard." He said: "I heard him say such and such," and he related to them what the Prophet (ﷺ) had said. Then Urwa ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi stood and said: "O people, are you not the father?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Am I not the father?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Do you accuse me?" They said: "No." He said: "Do you not know that I called up the people of Ukaz, and when they hesitated with me, I brought you my family, my children, and whoever obeyed me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Indeed this man has offered you a path of right guidance, so accept it, and let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." So he went to him and began speaking with the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him something similar to what he had said to Budayl. Then Urwa said: "O Muhammad, do you think that if you uproot your people, you have heard of any Arab who destroyed his own origin before you? And if the other happens, by Allah, I see faces and rabble of people who I think will flee and abandon you." Abu Bakr said: "Suck the clitoris of al-Lat!" Al-Lat was the idol of Thaqif that they used to worship. "Will we flee and abandon him?" Urwa said: "Who is this?" They said: "Abu Bakr." He said: "As for Him in whose hand is my soul, were it not for a favour you had upon me, I would not have repaid you for it, I would have answered you." Then he began speaking with the Prophet (ﷺ), and whenever he spoke to him, he took hold of his beard, while al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba was standing at the head of the Prophet (ﷺ) with a sword and wearing a helmet. Whenever Urwa reached toward the beard of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he struck his hand with the edge of the sword and said: "Remove your hand from his beard!" He raised his head and said: "Who is this?" They said: "al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba." He said: "O treacherous one! Am I not trying to remedy your treachery?" Al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba had accompanied a group of people in the Jahiliyya, killed them, and taken their wealth, then came and embraced Islam. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "As for Islam, we have accepted it; as for the wealth, it is wealth of treachery, and we have no need for it." Urwa began glancing at the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) with his eye. By Allah, whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) spat a spittle, it would fall into the palm of one of them, and he would rub it over his face and skin. When he commanded them, they rushed to carry out his command; when he performed ablution, they almost fought over his ablution water; when he spoke, they lowered their voices in his presence, and they did not stare at him out of reverence for him. Urwa returned to his companions and said: "O people, by Allah, I have visited kings. I have visited Caesar, Khosrow, and the Negus. By Allah, I have never seen a king whom his companions honour as the companions of Muhammad honour Muhammad. By Allah, if he spits a spittle, it falls into the palm of one of them, and he rubs it over his face and skin; when he commands them, they rush to carry out his command; when he performs ablution, they almost fight over his ablution water; when they speak in his presence, they lower their voices, and they do not stare at him out of reverence for him. Indeed he has offered you a path of right guidance, so accept it."

A man from Kinana said: "Let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." When he came close to the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "This is so-and-so, and he is from a people who honour the camels (al-budn), so send them to him." They sent them to him, and people came to meet him making the talbiya. When he saw that, he said: "Glory be to Allah! It is not right that these should be barred from the House." Then a man among them called Mikraz ibn Hafs stood and said: "Let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." When he came close to the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "This is Mikraz ibn Hafs, and he is a wicked man." He came and began speaking with the Prophet (ﷺ). While he was speaking to him, Suhayl ibn Amr came. Ayyub said, Ikrima said: When Suhayl came, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Your affair has been made easy for you." Al-Zuhri said: Suhayl ibn Amr came and said: "Come, let us write a document between us and you." So he called the scribe, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Write: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." He said: "What is 'the Most Merciful'? By Allah, I do not know what it is. Rather, write: 'In Your name, O Allah, as you used to write.'" The Muslims said: "By Allah, we will not write it except as 'In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.'" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Write: 'In Your name, O Allah.'" Then he said: "Write: 'This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed upon.'" Suhayl said: "By Allah, if we knew you were the Messenger of Allah, we would not have barred you from the House, nor fought you. But write: 'Muhammad ibn Abd Allah.'" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, I am indeed the Messenger of Allah, even if you deny me. But write: 'Muhammad ibn Abd Allah.'" Al-Zuhri said: That was [in accordance with] his words: "By Allah, they will not ask me for any arrangement by which they glorify the sacred things of Allah except that I will give it to them." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On condition that you leave the way clear between us and the House, so that we may circumambulate it." Suhayl said: "By Allah, the Arabs will not say that we were forced into submission, but [we will grant it] to you for the coming year." So it was written. Then Suhayl said: "And on condition that no man will come to you from us, if he is upon your religion, except that you return him to us." The Muslims said: "Glory be to Allah! How can he be returned to the polytheists when he has come as a Muslim?" While they were in that state, suddenly Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl ibn Amr came, dragging his feet in his shackles, having come out from the lower part of Mecca until he threw himself among the Muslims. Suhayl said: "O Muhammad, this is the first one for whom I contract with you that you return him to us." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Then grant him protection for me." He said: "I will not grant him protection for you." He said: "Yes, do so." He said: "I will not do so." His companion Mikraz said, while Suhayl was at his side: "We have granted him protection for you." Then Abu Jandal said: "O company of Muslims, am I to be returned to the polytheists when I have come as a Muslim? Do you not see what I have suffered? He had been tortured with severe torture for the sake of Allah."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 48, verse 25 (part 2 of 2):

"Umar ibn al-Khattab said: By God, I have never doubted since I embraced Islam except on that day. So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'Are we not upon the truth and our enemy upon falsehood?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Then why are we given the humiliation in our religion?' He said: 'I am the Messenger of God, and I will not disobey Him, and He is my helper.' I said: 'Did you not tell us that we would come to the House (the Ka'bah) and circumambulate it?' He said: 'Yes. Did I tell you that you would come to it this year?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Then you will come to it and circumambulate it.'"

"He said: Then I came to Abu Bakr and said: 'Is this not the Prophet of God in truth?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Are we not upon the truth and our enemy upon falsehood?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Then why are we given the humiliation in our religion?' He said: 'O man, he is the Messenger of God, and he does not disobey his Lord. Hold fast to his stirrup until you die, for by God he is upon the truth.' I said: 'Did he not used to tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?' He said: 'Yes. Did I tell you that you would come to it this year?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Then you will come to it and circumambulate it.'"

Al-Zuhri said: Umar said: "So I did righteous deeds on account of that." When the Prophet (ﷺ) had finished his account, he said to his companions: "Arise, sacrifice, then shave your heads." He said: "By God, not a man of us stood up until he said that three times. When none of them stood up, he went and entered upon Umm Salamah and mentioned to her what he had encountered from the people. Umm Salamah said: 'O Messenger of God, do you wish for that? Go out, and do not speak a single word to any of them until you sacrifice your camel and call your barber so that he shaves you.' So he went out and did not speak a word to any of them until he sacrificed his camel and called his barber, and he shaved him. When they saw that, they stood up and sacrificed, and some of them began shaving others, until some of them nearly killed one another out of grief." Then believing women came to him, and God, mighty and majestic, revealed to him: ﴿O you who believe, when believing women come to you as emigrants﴾ until ﴿the disbelieving wives﴾. He said: "So Umar that day divorced two women who had been his wives in polytheism." He said: "He forbade them to return the women and commanded them to return the dowries at that time." A man said to al-Zuhri: "Was that for the sake of the private parts?" He said: "Yes." One of them (the two women) was then married by Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, and the other by Safwan ibn Umayyah.

Then the Prophet (ﷺ) returned to Medina, and Abu Basir, a man of Quraysh, who was a Muslim, came to him. Two men were sent in pursuit of him and said: "The covenant that you made for us." So he handed him over to the two men, and they set out with him until, when they reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, they dismounted and ate some dates they had. Abu Basir said to one of the two men: "By God, I see that your sword, O so-and-so, is fine." The other drew it and said: "By God, it is indeed fine; I have tested it and been tested by it." Abu Basir said: "Show me, let me look at it," and he gave it to him. He struck him with it until he was cold, and the other fled until he reached Medina and entered the mosque running. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, seeing him in terror: "This one has seen fear." He said: "By God, my companion has been killed, and I, by God, am about to be killed." Then Abu Basir came and said: "By God, God has fulfilled your covenant, you returned me to them, then God rescued me from them." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Woe to his mother! He is a kindler of war, if only he had some support." When he heard that, he understood that he would return him to them. So he went out until he reached the seashore. Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl ibn Amr escaped and joined Abu Basir. No man of Quraysh who had embraced Islam went out without joining Abu Basir, until a band of them gathered. By God, they did not hear of a caravan of Quraysh going out to Syria without intercepting them, killing them, and taking their wealth. Then Quraysh sent to the Prophet (ﷺ) pleading with him by God and by kinship to send for them, and whoever came to him would be safe. So God revealed ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them﴾ until ﴿the zealotry of ignorance﴾. Their zealotry was that they did not acknowledge that he was a prophet, nor did they acknowledge ﴿In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾, and they prevented them from reaching the House."

⁕ Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan ibn al-Hakam, who both said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) went out during al-Hudaybiyah with some hundreds (more than a thousand), then he mentioned something similar, except that in his narration he said: Al-Zuhri said: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad told me that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) said: "So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'Are you not the Messenger of God (ﷺ)?' He said: 'Yes.'" He also said: "Abu Basir and those who had embraced Islam from those whom the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had sent back went out until they joined the coast on the route of the caravan of Quraysh, and they killed those disbelievers in it and seized its goods. When the disbelievers of Quraysh saw that, a group of them rode to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said to him: 'Your term does not benefit us at all; we are being killed and our wealth is being plundered. We ask you to include these people among those who have embraced Islam from us in your treaty, and to protect them, and to restrain us from fighting them.' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) did that, and God revealed: ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them﴾." Then he related the hadith to its end, similar to the hadith of Ibn Abd al-A'la.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan ibn al-Hakam, that they both told him: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) went out in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, intending to visit the House, not intending fighting, and he took with him his sacrificial animals, seventy camels. When he reached Usfan, Bishr ibn Sufyan al-Ka'bi met him and said to him: 'O Messenger of God, these are the Quraysh; they have heard of your march, so they have gone out with them the al-'Awdh al-Mataafil, having put on leopard skins, and they have camped at Dhu Tuwa, swearing by God that you will never enter upon them. This is Khalid ibn al-Walid with their cavalry, who have advanced them to Kura al-Ghamim.'" He said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Woe to Quraysh! War has indeed destroyed them. What would it cost them if they left me between myself and the rest of the Arabs? If they harm me, that is what they wanted; and if God makes me victorious over them, they will enter Islam humbled.'" Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ma'mar with many additions, which I have left out, since they are in addition to the hadith of Ma'mar.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿And the sacrificial animals detained from reaching their place of sacrifice﴾: "The sacrificial animals were at Dhu Tuwa, and al-Hudaybiyah is outside the sacred precinct (haram). The Messenger of God (ﷺ) camped there when Quraysh had cut off the water from him."
