Concerning His words ﴿And were it not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, that you might trample them, and there would befall you because of them a difficulty without knowledge﴾:

He, may He be exalted, says: Were it not for men among the people of faith and women among them, O believers in God, whom you would trample with your horses and your feet, and you did not know them in Mecca, and the polytheists had held them there away from you, so that because of that they could not come out to you and you would kill them.

As follows:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿And were it not for believing men and believing women﴾ ... until ﴿without knowledge﴾: "This was when Muhammad and his companions were prevented from entering Mecca. There were believing men and believing women in it, and God disliked that they be harmed or trampled without knowledge, so that a difficulty would befall you from them without knowledge."

The interpreters of the Qur'an differed concerning the difficulty (ma'arrah) that God intended in this place. Some of them said: it means sin.

Those who said that:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words (And were it not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, that you might trample them, and there would befall you because of them a difficulty without knowledge): "A sin without knowledge."

Others said: it means the payment of blood money (diyah).

Those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, concerning ﴿and there would befall you because of them a difficulty without knowledge﴾: "that you would pay their blood money. As for sin, He did not count it against them." The ma'arrah is the mif'alah from al-'arr, which is mange, and the meaning is: there would befall you from their side a difficulty by which you would be stricken, obligating you because of it the expiation for accidental killing, which is freeing a believing slave, for whoever is able to do so, and whoever is not able, then fasting two months.

I chose this view over the view stated by Ibn Ishaq because God only obligated, upon the one who kills a believer in the land of war if he had not emigrated from it, and his killer did not know his faith, the expiation rather than the blood money. He said: ﴿And if he is from a people hostile to you and he is a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave﴾. He did not obligate for the accidental killing of such a person the blood money. Therefore we say that the ma'arrah in this place means the expiation. And the ﴿an﴾ in His words ﴿that you might trample them﴾ is in the nominative position, in response to the men, because the meaning of the statement is: "Were it not that you would trample men who are believers and women who are believers, whom you did not know, so that a difficulty would befall you from them without knowledge, God would have permitted you, O believers, to enter Mecca. But He prevented you from that." ﴿That God may admit into His mercy whom He wills﴾ means: that God may admit into Islam from the people of Mecca whom He wills before you enter it. The answer to "were it not" has been omitted, being indicated by the context.

* *

Concerning His words ﴿If they had been separated﴾:

It means: If those among the polytheists of Mecca who were believing men and believing women, whom you did not know among them, had been distinguished, and separated from them, and gone out from among them, ﴿We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment﴾. That is: We would have killed those remaining in it by the sword, or destroyed them with some of what would cause them pain from Our swift punishment.

The interpreters of the Qur'an said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿If they had been separated﴾ ... the verse: "God repels the disbelievers through the believers."

⁕ I was told, from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, who said: He heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words ﴿If they had been separated, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them﴾, meaning the people of Mecca, among whom were believers who were oppressed: God says, "Were it not for those oppressed ones, if they had been separated, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment."

⁕ Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿If they had been separated﴾: "If they had dispersed, so that the believer was separated from the disbeliever, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment."

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His mention: ﴿When those who disbelieved had placed in their hearts zealotry — the zealotry of ignorance — then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers and obligated them to the word of righteousness, and they were more deserving of it and worthy of it. And Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾ (26)

He, exalted is His mention, means by His saying ﴿When those who disbelieved had placed in their hearts zealotry — the zealotry of ignorance﴾: when Suhayl ibn 'Amr placed zealotry in his heart, so he refused to have written in the treaty document, which was written in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the polytheists, "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful," and refused to have written in it, "Muhammad, Messenger of Allah." He and his people also refused to let the Messenger of Allah ﷺ enter in that year.

The exegetes said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, who said: Their zealotry, which Allah mentioned, "when those who disbelieved had placed in their hearts zealotry, the zealotry of ignorance," was that they did not acknowledge "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful," and they barred them from the House.

- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, with something similar.

- 'Amr ibn Muhammad al-'Uthmani narrated to me, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Uways narrated to us, saying: my brother narrated to me, from Sulayman, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that Abu Hurayrah informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, 'There is no deity but Allah.' Whoever says, 'There is no deity but Allah,' has protected his property and his self from me, except by its right, and his reckoning is with Allah." And Allah revealed in His Book, mentioning a people who were arrogant, saying: ﴿Indeed, they, when it was said to them, "There is no deity but Allah," were arrogant﴾, and Allah said: ﴿When those who disbelieved had placed in their hearts zealotry — the zealotry of ignorance — then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers and obligated them to the word of righteousness, and they were more deserving of it and worthy of it﴾. And it is: "There is no deity but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," which the polytheists were arrogant towards on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, the day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made the treaty with them for the period of truce.

As for "idh" in His saying ﴿When those who disbelieved﴾, it is connected to His saying: "We would have punished." The meaning of the statement: "We would have punished those among them who disbelieved with a painful punishment, when those who disbelieved had placed in their hearts zealotry." Al-hamiyyah is of the form fa'iliyyah from the speaker's saying: "Fulan protected his nose (hamā anfahu) with zealotry (ḥamiyyah) and protection (muḥammiyah)." From it is the saying of al-Mutalammis:

Indeed I am among them, and my honour is their honour,
Just as the head protects its nose from being cut off.

[The verse is by al-Mutalammis Jarir ibn 'Abd al-Masih. "Kashama anfahu" means he cut off his nose entirely. Fulan is "dhu hamiyyah munkarah" when he is full of anger and pride.]

By His saying "yahmi" he means: prevents. And He said ﴿zealotry of ignorance﴾ because what they did of that was entirely from the characteristics of the people of disbelief, and none of it was something Allah permitted them, nor any of His messengers.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: Allah sent down patience, calm and dignity upon His Messenger and upon the believers, when those who disbelieved were zealous with the zealotry of ignorance, and they prevented them from circumambulating the House, and refused to write in the document between Him and them, "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful," and "Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." ﴿And obligated them to the word of righteousness﴾: it is said: He obligated them to the statement "There is no deity but Allah," by which they guard themselves against the Fire and the painful punishment.

The exegetes said things similar to what we have said on this matter, with differences among them, and the report was narrated with it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Mention of those who said that in accordance with what we have said, and the report we mentioned from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:

- al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Habib narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Thawr ibn Abi Fakhitah, from his father, from al-Tufayl, from his father, who heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say ﴿and obligated them to the word of righteousness﴾, and he said: "There is no deity but Allah."

- Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Khidash al-'Ataki narrated to me, saying: I heard Salim, who heard Shu'bah, who heard Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who heard 'Abayah, who heard 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning His saying ﴿and obligated them to the word of righteousness﴾, he said: There is no deity but Allah.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to me, saying: Yahya and 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah, from 'Abayah ibn Rib'i, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning His saying ﴿and obligated them to the word of righteousness﴾, he said: There is no deity but Allah, and Allah is greatest.

- Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Damghani narrated to me, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Sufyan and Shu'bah, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from a man, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: There is no deity but Allah, and Allah is greatest.

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Salamah, from 'Abayah, from a man of Banu Tamim, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, ﴿and obligated them to the word of righteousness﴾, he said: There is no deity but Allah.

- 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿and obligated them to the word of righteousness﴾, he said: the testimony that there is no deity but Allah; so it is the word of righteousness, he said: it is the head of righteousness.

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Ishaq narrate from 'Amr ibn Maymun that he used to say concerning this verse ﴿and obligated them to the word of righteousness﴾, he said: There is no deity but Allah.

- Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: Sufyan informed me, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, the like of it.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun ﴿and obligated them to the word of righteousness﴾, he said: There is no deity but Allah.

- Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid ﴿and obligated them to the word of righteousness﴾, he said: There is no deity but Allah.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah ﴿and obligated them to the word of righteousness﴾, and it is: the testimony that there is no deity but Allah.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿and obligated them to the word of righteousness﴾, he said: it is "There is no deity but Allah."

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying ﴿and obligated them to the word of righteousness﴾: it is "There is no deity but Allah."

- Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Hafs ibn 'Umar narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, concerning His saying ﴿and obligated them to the word of righteousness﴾, he said: the testimony that there is no deity but Allah.

- Ibn al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani ﴿and obligated them to the word of righteousness﴾, he said: There is no deity but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.

- al-Sawwari Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sawwar narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Khalid al-Makki, from 'Ali al-Azdi, who said: I was with Ibn 'Umar between Makkah and Mina at al-Ma'zimayn, and he heard the people saying: "There is no deity but Allah, and Allah is greatest." He said: "It is it, it is it." I said: "What is it?" He said, ﴿and obligated them to the word of righteousness﴾: the sincerity (al-ikhlas), ﴿and they were more deserving of it and worthy of it﴾.

Others said: Rather, it is the word of righteousness, sincerity.

Mention of those who said that:

- 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Azdi narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid ﴿and obligated them to the word of righteousness﴾, he said: the sincerity.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿the word of righteousness﴾: the word of sincerity.

Others said: It is His saying: "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful."

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, concerning His saying ﴿and obligated them to the word of righteousness﴾, he said: "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful."

Others said: It is the saying: "There is no deity but Allah, alone, without partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things Capable."

Mention of those who said that:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, from Mujahid and 'Ata' ﴿and obligated them to the word of righteousness﴾, he said: one of them said it is the sincerity, and the other said: the word of righteousness: "There is no deity but Allah, alone, without partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things Capable."

* *

As for His saying ﴿and they were more deserving of it and worthy of it﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the believers were more deserving of the word of righteousness than the polytheists, and worthy of it; that is, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the believers were the people of the word of righteousness, to the exclusion of the polytheists.

It is mentioned that in the recitation of 'Abd Allah it is: ﴿and they were worthy of it and more deserving of it﴾.

The exegetes said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah ﴿and they were more deserving of it and worthy of it﴾: the Muslims were more deserving of it and worthy of it, namely the Tawhid, and the testimony that there is no deity but Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: Allah has never ceased to have knowledge of all things, nothing is hidden from Him of what exists; and by His knowledge, O people, of what would occur from your entering Makkah while there are believing men and believing women among them whom you did not know, He did not permit you to enter Makkah on this journey of yours.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 48, verse 27:

On the interpretation of His words, ﴿Indeed, Allah fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth. You will surely enter al-Masjid al-Haram, if Allah wills, in security, with your heads shaved and [your hair] shortened, not fearing anyone.  So He knew what you did not know and has arranged, besides that, an imminent conquest.﴾ (48:27)

He, exalted is He, says: Allah has indeed fulfilled for His Messenger Muhammad the vision which He showed him, that he and his companions would enter the Sacred House of Allah in security, not fearing the people of polytheism, some of them having their heads shaved and some having them shortened.

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the like of what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, who said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Indeed, Allah fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth: you will surely enter al-Masjid al-Haram, if Allah wills, in security﴾ He said: it is the entry of Muhammad (ﷺ) into the House, and the believers, with their heads shaved and shortened.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, who said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, who said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, who said: al-Hasan narrated to us, who said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿the vision in truth﴾, he said: It was shown to him at al-Hudaybiyah that he would enter Makkah and his companions would be shaved. Then his companions, when he slaughtered at al-Hudaybiyah, said: Where is the vision of Muhammad (ﷺ)?

* Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Indeed, Allah fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth﴾, he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw that he was circumambulating the House with his companions, so Allah fulfilled his vision, and said ﴿You will surely enter al-Masjid al-Haram, if Allah wills, in security﴾ ... until ﴿not fearing﴾.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, who said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, Allah fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth﴾, he said: It was shown to him in a dream that they would enter al-Masjid al-Haram, and that they would be secure, with their heads shaved and shortened.

* Yunus narrated to us, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, Allah fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth﴾ ... to the end of the verse. He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: "I have seen that you will enter al-Masjid al-Haram with your heads shaved and shortened." When he arrived at al-Hudaybiyah and did not enter that year, the hypocrites criticised this, saying: Where is his vision? Then Allah said ﴿Indeed, Allah fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth﴾, and recited until ﴿and shortened, not fearing﴾. "I did not see him entering it this year, but it will certainly happen."

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, ﴿Indeed, Allah fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth⁠﴾ ... to His words ﴿if Allah wills, in security﴾, regarding the vision of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) which was shown to him, that he would enter Makkah secure, not fearing. He says: with heads shaved and shortened, not fearing.

* *

And His words ﴿So He knew what you did not know﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Allah, may His praise be exalted, knew what you did not know, and that was His knowledge, exalted is His remembrance, of the believing men and women who were in Makkah, whom the believers did not know. Had they entered it that year, they would have trampled upon them with horses and on foot, and harm would have befallen them from them without knowledge, so Allah turned them back from Makkah for that reason.

And the people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿So He knew what you did not know﴾, he said: He turned them back because of the believing men and women who were among them, and delayed it so that Allah might admit into His mercy whom He wills, of those who He wants to guide.

* *

And His words ﴿and has arranged, besides that, an imminent conquest﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding the imminent conquest which Allah made for the believers, besides their entering al-Masjid al-Haram with heads shaved and shortened. Some of them said: It is the truce which took place between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the polytheists of Quraysh.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, who said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, who said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, who said: al-Hasan narrated to us, who said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿besides that, an imminent conquest﴾, he said: The slaughter at al-Hudaybiyah; then they returned and conquered Khaybar, then he performed 'umrah after that, and the fulfilment of his vision was in the following year.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, regarding His words ﴿besides that, an imminent conquest﴾, meaning: the truce of al-Hudaybiyah. Nothing conquered in Islam was greater than it. Fighting only happened wherever people met; but when the truce came, war was laid down, and all people were secure from one another, so they met and conversed and debated, and no one who spoke to anyone about Islam, if he understood anything, failed to enter it. Indeed, in those two years there entered Islam as many as had entered it before, and more.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding His words ﴿an imminent conquest﴾, he said: the truce of al-Hudaybiyah.

Others said: By the imminent conquest in this place is meant the conquest of Khaybar.

Mention of those who said that:

* Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿besides that, an imminent conquest﴾, he said: Khaybar, when they returned from al-Hudaybiyah; Allah conquered it for them, and divided it among all the people of al-Hudaybiyah except one man from the Ansar, called Abu Dujanah Simak ibn Kharashah, who had witnessed al-Hudaybiyah but was absent from Khaybar.

The most correct of these sayings is that it should be said: Allah informed that He made for His Messenger and those who were with him from among the people of the Pledge of Good Pleasure (bay'at al-ridwan) a conquest imminent, besides their entering al-Masjid al-Haram and besides His fulfilling the vision of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The truce of al-Hudaybiyah and the conquest of Khaybar were beneath that, and Allah, exalted is His remembrance, did not specify His report of that as a conquest of one kind rather than another, but generalised it, and all of that is a conquest which Allah made besides that.

And the correct view is to generalise it as He generalised it, so it is said: Allah made, besides His fulfilling the vision of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of his entering with his companions al-Masjid al-Haram with heads shaved and shortened, not fearing the polytheists, the truce of al-Hudaybiyah and the conquest of Khaybar.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 48, verses 28–29 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, and sufficient is Allah as Witness.﴾ (28) ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and approval. Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration. That is their description in the Torah. And their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot and strengthens it, so it grows firm and stands on its stalk, pleasing the sowers, that He may enrage by them the disbelievers. Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ (29)

His, the Exalted's, saying ﴿It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth﴾ means: He who sent His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ with clear proof and the religion of truth, which is Islam, sending him as a caller of His creation to it. ﴿That He may make it prevail over all religion﴾ means: that He may nullify by it all other creeds, so that there is no religion besides it. This will remain so until 'Isa (Jesus) son of Maryam descends, kills the Dajjal (Antichrist), and then all religions will be nullified except the religion of Allah with which Muhammad ﷺ was sent, and Islam will prevail over all religions.
* *
As for His saying ﴿and sufficient is Allah as Witness﴾:
He, may His praise be exalted, says to His Prophet ﷺ: "I have made your Lord, O Muhammad, bear witness on His own behalf that He will make prevail the religion with which He has sent you." ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Witness﴾ means: and sufficient is He as a witness for you.
Those among the people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.
Mention of those who said this:
- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali related to us, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, and sufficient is Allah as Witness﴾: He says, "I bear witness for you on His own behalf that He will make your religion prevail over all religion." This is an announcement from Allah, the Exalted, to His Prophet ﷺ, and to those among his companions who disliked the peace treaty on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, that Allah will open Makkah and other lands to them, consoling them thereby for what had befallen them of grief and sorrow, through their turning back from Makkah before entering it and before circumambulating the House.
* *
As for His saying ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves﴾:
He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those who follow him among his companions who are upon his religion, ﴿forceful against the disbelievers﴾, their hearts harsh toward them, their mercy toward them little; ﴿merciful among themselves﴾ means: tender-hearted toward one another, gentle in their souls toward each other, lenient toward one another.
As:
- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿merciful among themselves﴾: Allah placed mercy in their hearts toward one another. ﴿You see them bowing and prostrating﴾ means: you see them bowing at times in their prayer, and prostrating at times. ﴿Seeking bounty from Allah﴾ means: they seek by their bowing and prostrating, and their harshness toward the disbelievers and their mercy toward one another, bounty from Allah, which is His mercy toward them, by His favouring them and admitting them into His Garden. ﴿And approval﴾ means: and that their Lord be pleased with them.
* *
As for His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾:
It means: their sign on their faces is from the trace of prostration in their prayer.
Then the people of interpretation differed concerning the sima (mark) that Allah means in this place. Some of them said: it is a sign which Allah places on the faces of the believers on the Day of Resurrection, by which they are recognized, because of their prostration to Him in this world.
Mention of those who said this:
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "Their prayer appears on their faces on the Day of Resurrection."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: 'Ubayd Allah al-'Ataki related to us, from Khalid al-Hanafi, regarding His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "That is recognized on the Day of Resurrection on their faces from the trace of their prostration in this world, and it is like His saying ﴿you recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss﴾."
- 'Ubayd ibn Asbat ibn Muhammad related to me, he said: my father related to us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from 'Atiyyah, regarding ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "The places of prostration on their faces on the Day of Resurrection are the whitest parts of their faces."
- Muhammad ibn 'Umarah related to us, he said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, he said: Ibn Fudayl informed us, from Fudayl, from 'Atiyyah, similarly.
- Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, he said: Ibn Fudayl related to us, from Fudayl, from 'Atiyyah, similarly.
- Mujahid ibn Musa related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Fudayl informed us, from 'Atiyyah, the like of it.
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: al-Mu'tamir related to us, he said: I heard Shabib say, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, he said: ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: "The light on the Day of Resurrection."
- Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz related to us, he said: Harun ibn Isma'il related to us, he said: 'Ali ibn al-Mubarak said: I heard more than one person, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "Whiteness in their faces on the Day of Resurrection."

Others said: rather, it is the mark of Islam, its bearing, its humility, and its submissiveness, and by this is meant that it is seen upon them in this world.
Mention of those who said this:
- 'Ali related to us, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Their mark is on their faces﴾: He said: "The good bearing."
- He said: Mujahid related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Mu'awiyah related to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "Indeed it is not what you see, but it is the mark of Islam, its complexion, its manner and its humility."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu 'Amir related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "Humility and modesty."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Mu'ammal related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Mujahid, similarly.
- He said: Abu 'Amir related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "Humility."
- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, from Shu'bah, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, regarding this verse ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "Complexion (sahnah)."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "It is humility." I said: "It is the trace of prostration?" He said: "It will be between his eyes like the knee of a goat, and it is as Allah wills."

Others said: it is a trace that appears on the faces of those who pray, like the trace of sleeplessness, which shows on the face as dark patches, redness and paleness, and similar things that wakefulness and fatigue show on the face. They interpreted it as a mark in this world.
Mention of those who said this:
- Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "Paleness."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: al-Mu'tamir related to us, from his father, he said: The shaykh who used to narrate stories in hardship claimed, and recited ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾, and he claimed it is the sleeplessness seen on their faces.
- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Ya'qub al-Qummi related to us, from Hafs, from Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah, regarding His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces﴾: He said: "Dark patches appear on the face from sleeplessness at night."

Others said: they are traces seen on the face from the dust of the earth, or the moisture of purification.
Mention of those who said this:
- Hawthara ibn Muhammad al-Minqari related to us, he said: Hammad ibn Mas'adah related to us; and Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, both from Thalabah ibn Suhayl, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "The dust of the earth and the moisture of purification."
- Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz related to us, he said: Harun ibn Isma'il related to us, he said: 'Ali ibn al-Mubarak related to us, he said: Malik ibn Dinar related to us, he said: I heard 'Ikrimah say, regarding ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: "It is the trace of dust."

The most correct of these sayings, in our view, is that it should be said: Allah, the Exalted, has informed us that the mark of these people whom He has described is on their faces from the trace of prostration, and He did not restrict it to one time over another. Since this is so, it applies at all times. So their mark by which they were recognized in this world was the trace of Islam, that is, its humility, its guidance, its asceticism and its bearing, and the traces of performing its obligations and its voluntary acts. And in the Hereafter, it is what He informed us they will be recognized by: the white blaze on the face and the white marks on the hands and feet from the trace of ablution, and the whiteness of faces from the trace of prostration.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of the sima (mark).
Mention of those who said this:
- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "Their sign, or the prayer has informed them."
* *
As for His saying ﴿That is their description in the Torah﴾:
He says: this quality which I have described to you of the followers of Muhammad ﷺ who are with him, is their description in the Torah.
* *
As for His saying ﴿And their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot﴾:
He says: their description in the Gospel of 'Isa is the description of a seed which produces its shoot (shat'ahu), which is its sprouts. It is said of it: the crop has sprouted (ash'ata al-zar'u) when it puts forth shoots, so it sprouts (yushti'u) ishta'. They were likened to the sprouting crop because they began to enter Islam while they were a small number, and then they kept increasing, and a group entered after them, then another group after that group, until their number grew, just as in the root of the crop a shoot comes forth, then another shoot after it, until it multiplies and grows.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.
Mention of those who said this:
- 'Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to us, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him﴾, his companions, their likeness, meaning their description written in the Torah and the Gospel before the heavens and the earth were created.
- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: 'Ubayd related to us, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers﴾ ... until His saying ﴿That is their description in the Torah﴾, then He said ﴿And their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot﴾ ... the verse.
- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, the same: ﴿That is their description in the Torah﴾: that is, this description is in the Torah. ﴿And their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot﴾: this is the description of the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Gospel.
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾, he said: ﴿That is their description in the Torah, and their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot﴾.
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration, that is their description in the Torah﴾: meaning the mark on the faces is their description in the Torah, and it is not their description in the Gospel. Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot﴾ ... the verse; this is their description in the Gospel.
- Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration, that is their description in the Torah, and their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot﴾.
- 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid related to me, he said: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him﴾ ... the verse; he said: "This is their description in the Torah, and another likeness in the Gospel: ﴿like a seed which produces its shoot, and strengthens it﴾ ... the verse."

Others said: these two likenesses are their description in the Torah and the Gospel.
Mention of those who said this:
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿That is their description in the Torah﴾: and the Gospel is the same.

The most correct of the two sayings, in our view, is the saying of the one who said: their likeness in the Torah is other than their likeness in the Gospel, and that the report about their likeness in the Torah ends at His saying ﴿That is their description in the Torah﴾. This is because if the matter were as Mujahid said, that their likeness in the Torah and the Gospel is one, the revelation would have been: "and their likeness in the Gospel, and like a seed which produces its shoot," so that the comparison with the seed would be conjoined to His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾, so that it would be a report that this is their likeness in the Torah and the Gospel. The absence of the conjunction "and" before His saying ﴿like a seed﴾ is clear evidence for the correctness of what we have said, and that the words ﴿And their description in the Gospel﴾ are a new statement about their quality which is in the Gospel, apart from what is in the Torah.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding His saying ﴿produces its shoot﴾.
Mention of those who said this:
- Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi related to me, he said: my father related to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Khaythamah, he said: While 'Abd Allah was teaching a man at sunset, he passed by this verse ﴿like a seed which produces its shoot﴾, and he said: "You are the crop, and your harvest has drawn near."
- He said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to us, he said: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Humayd al-Tawil, he said: Anas ibn Malik recited ﴿like a seed which produces its shoot, and strengthens it﴾, and said: "Do you know what its shoot is?" He said: "Its growth."
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿That is their description in the Torah, and their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot﴾: He said: "Its spike when its growth separates from its grain."
- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot﴾: He said: "This is the likeness of the companions of Muhammad ﷺ in the Gospel. It was said to them: a people will come forth who will grow like the growth of the crop, among them people who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah and al-Zuhri, regarding ﴿like a seed which produces its shoot﴾: both said: "It brought forth its growth."
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿And their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot﴾: meaning: the companions of Muhammad ﷺ, who will be few, then they will increase, multiply and grow strong.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 48, verse 28–29 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿like a seed that sends out its shoot﴾: "Its offspring; then its offspring multiplied."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿like a seed that sends out its shoot﴾: He said: "That which comes out beside the furrow, and it is completed and grows."

* *

As for His words ﴿so it strengthens it﴾:
It means: it strengthens it, i.e., the shoot strengthens the seed and helps it. It is from al-muwazarah (المؤازرة), which means mutual assistance (المعاونة). ﴿Then it becomes thick﴾ means: the seed becomes thick. ﴿So it stands firm upon its stalk﴾. Al-suwq (السوق) is the plural of saq (ساق), and the saq of a crop or tree is that which bears it.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.
Those who said so:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿so it strengthens it﴾: "Its growth together with its intertwining when it puts forth ears of grain." ﴿That is their likeness in the Torah, and their likeness in the Gospel﴾: It is a parable that He struck for the People of the Book: when a people emerge growing as the crop grows, and men arise among them who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and then they become strong, and they are those who were with them. It is also a parable that Allah struck for Muhammad ﷺ. He says: Allah sent the Prophet alone, then a small number gathered to him believing in him, then the few become many and grow strong, and Allah enrages the disbelievers through them.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿so it strengthens it﴾: He said: "It strengthened it and helped it."

* *

As for His words ﴿upon its stalk﴾:
He said: its roots.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah and al-Zuhri, regarding ﴿so it strengthens it, so it becomes thick, so it stands firm upon its stalk﴾: He says: "It joins together."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿so it strengthens it﴾: "It gathered together and became intertwined." He said: Likewise the believers went out while they were few and weak, and Allah continued to increase them and support them with Islam, just as He supported this seed with its offspring, so it strengthened it, and it became a parable for the believers.

⁕ Amr ibn Abd al-Hamid narrated to me, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿like a seed that sends out its shoot, so it strengthens it, so it becomes thick, so it stands firm upon its stalk﴾: He says: "A grain of wheat scattered and dispersed, so each grain sprouts one stalk, then each one of them sprouts, until it becomes thick and stands firm upon its stalk." He said: He says: The companions of Muhammad ﷺ were few, then they increased, then they became strong. ﴿That He may enrage﴾ Allah ﴿by them the disbelievers﴾.

* *

As for His words ﴿it pleases the sowers, that He may enrage by them the disbelievers﴾:
The Exalted, may His remembrance be praised, says: This crop that became thick and stood firm upon its stalk pleases those who sowed it with its completeness, its fine growth, and its reaching maturity and completion. ﴿That He may enrage by them the disbelievers﴾: He says: Likewise is the likeness of Muhammad ﷺ and his companions, and the gathering of their number until they increased and grew, and their affair became strong, like this crop whose description the Majestic One, may His praise be exalted, has described. Then He said ﴿that He may enrage by them the disbelievers﴾, which indicates an omitted part of the speech, namely that Allah did this with Muhammad ﷺ and his companions in order to enrage the disbelievers through them.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.
Those who said so:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿that He may enrage by them the disbelievers﴾: Allah says: Their likeness is like the likeness of a seed that sent out its shoot, so it strengthened it, so it became thick, so it stood firm upon its stalk, until it reached the finest growth, pleasing the sowers by its abundance and fine growth.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿it pleases the sowers﴾: "It pleases the sowers with its beauty." ﴿That He may enrage by them the disbelievers﴾: "By the believers, because of their multiplication. So this is their likeness in the Gospel."

* *

As for His words ﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them forgiveness and a great reward﴾:
The Exalted, may His remembrance be praised, says: Allah has promised those who affirmed Allah and His Messenger ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾, meaning: they acted upon what Allah commanded them of His obligations which He made binding upon them.

* *

As for His words ﴿among them﴾:
It means: from among the shoot which the seed sent out, namely those who entered Islam after the seed which our Lord, blessed and exalted is He, described. The pronoun "them" (هم) in His words ﴿among them﴾ refers to the meaning of the shoot, not its wording, and therefore it is stated in the plural "minhum" and not "minhu." The shoot is mentioned in the plural because what is intended is those who enter the religion of Muhammad ﷺ until the Day of Resurrection, after the group whose description Allah gave in His words ﴿and those with him are severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves; you see them bowing and prostrating﴾.

* *

As for His words ﴿and forgiveness﴾:
It means: pardon for what has passed of their sins and their evil deeds, by replacing them with good.

* *

As for His words ﴿and a great reward﴾:
It means: and an abundant reward, and that is Paradise.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Fath.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 48, verses 28–29 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, and sufficient is Allah as Witness.﴾ (28) ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and approval. Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration. That is their description in the Torah. And their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot and strengthens it, so it grows firm and stands on its stalk, pleasing the sowers, that He may enrage by them the disbelievers. Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ (29)

His, the Exalted's, saying ﴿It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth﴾ means: He who sent His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ with clear proof and the religion of truth, which is Islam, sending him as a caller of His creation to it. ﴿That He may make it prevail over all religion﴾ means: that He may nullify by it all other creeds, so that there is no religion besides it. This will remain so until 'Isa (Jesus) son of Maryam descends, kills the Dajjal (Antichrist), and then all religions will be nullified except the religion of Allah with which Muhammad ﷺ was sent, and Islam will prevail over all religions.
* *
As for His saying ﴿and sufficient is Allah as Witness﴾:
He, may His praise be exalted, says to His Prophet ﷺ: "I have made your Lord, O Muhammad, bear witness on His own behalf that He will make prevail the religion with which He has sent you." ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Witness﴾ means: and sufficient is He as a witness for you.
Those among the people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.
Mention of those who said this:
- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali related to us, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, and sufficient is Allah as Witness﴾: He says, "I bear witness for you on His own behalf that He will make your religion prevail over all religion." This is an announcement from Allah, the Exalted, to His Prophet ﷺ, and to those among his companions who disliked the peace treaty on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, that Allah will open Makkah and other lands to them, consoling them thereby for what had befallen them of grief and sorrow, through their turning back from Makkah before entering it and before circumambulating the House.
* *
As for His saying ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves﴾:
He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those who follow him among his companions who are upon his religion, ﴿forceful against the disbelievers﴾, their hearts harsh toward them, their mercy toward them little; ﴿merciful among themselves﴾ means: tender-hearted toward one another, gentle in their souls toward each other, lenient toward one another.
As:
- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿merciful among themselves﴾: Allah placed mercy in their hearts toward one another. ﴿You see them bowing and prostrating﴾ means: you see them bowing at times in their prayer, and prostrating at times. ﴿Seeking bounty from Allah﴾ means: they seek by their bowing and prostrating, and their harshness toward the disbelievers and their mercy toward one another, bounty from Allah, which is His mercy toward them, by His favouring them and admitting them into His Garden. ﴿And approval﴾ means: and that their Lord be pleased with them.
* *
As for His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾:
It means: their sign on their faces is from the trace of prostration in their prayer.
Then the people of interpretation differed concerning the sima (mark) that Allah means in this place. Some of them said: it is a sign which Allah places on the faces of the believers on the Day of Resurrection, by which they are recognized, because of their prostration to Him in this world.
Mention of those who said this:
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "Their prayer appears on their faces on the Day of Resurrection."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: 'Ubayd Allah al-'Ataki related to us, from Khalid al-Hanafi, regarding His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "That is recognized on the Day of Resurrection on their faces from the trace of their prostration in this world, and it is like His saying ﴿you recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss﴾."
- 'Ubayd ibn Asbat ibn Muhammad related to me, he said: my father related to us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from 'Atiyyah, regarding ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "The places of prostration on their faces on the Day of Resurrection are the whitest parts of their faces."
- Muhammad ibn 'Umarah related to us, he said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, he said: Ibn Fudayl informed us, from Fudayl, from 'Atiyyah, similarly.
- Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, he said: Ibn Fudayl related to us, from Fudayl, from 'Atiyyah, similarly.
- Mujahid ibn Musa related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Fudayl informed us, from 'Atiyyah, the like of it.
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: al-Mu'tamir related to us, he said: I heard Shabib say, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, he said: ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: "The light on the Day of Resurrection."
- Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz related to us, he said: Harun ibn Isma'il related to us, he said: 'Ali ibn al-Mubarak said: I heard more than one person, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "Whiteness in their faces on the Day of Resurrection."

Others said: rather, it is the mark of Islam, its bearing, its humility, and its submissiveness, and by this is meant that it is seen upon them in this world.
Mention of those who said this:
- 'Ali related to us, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Their mark is on their faces﴾: He said: "The good bearing."
- He said: Mujahid related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Mu'awiyah related to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "Indeed it is not what you see, but it is the mark of Islam, its complexion, its manner and its humility."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu 'Amir related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "Humility and modesty."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Mu'ammal related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Mujahid, similarly.
- He said: Abu 'Amir related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "Humility."
- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, from Shu'bah, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, regarding this verse ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "Complexion (sahnah)."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "It is humility." I said: "It is the trace of prostration?" He said: "It will be between his eyes like the knee of a goat, and it is as Allah wills."

Others said: it is a trace that appears on the faces of those who pray, like the trace of sleeplessness, which shows on the face as dark patches, redness and paleness, and similar things that wakefulness and fatigue show on the face. They interpreted it as a mark in this world.
Mention of those who said this:
- Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "Paleness."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: al-Mu'tamir related to us, from his father, he said: The shaykh who used to narrate stories in hardship claimed, and recited ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾, and he claimed it is the sleeplessness seen on their faces.
- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Ya'qub al-Qummi related to us, from Hafs, from Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah, regarding His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces﴾: He said: "Dark patches appear on the face from sleeplessness at night."

Others said: they are traces seen on the face from the dust of the earth, or the moisture of purification.
Mention of those who said this:
- Hawthara ibn Muhammad al-Minqari related to us, he said: Hammad ibn Mas'adah related to us; and Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, both from Thalabah ibn Suhayl, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "The dust of the earth and the moisture of purification."
- Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz related to us, he said: Harun ibn Isma'il related to us, he said: 'Ali ibn al-Mubarak related to us, he said: Malik ibn Dinar related to us, he said: I heard 'Ikrimah say, regarding ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: "It is the trace of dust."

The most correct of these sayings, in our view, is that it should be said: Allah, the Exalted, has informed us that the mark of these people whom He has described is on their faces from the trace of prostration, and He did not restrict it to one time over another. Since this is so, it applies at all times. So their mark by which they were recognized in this world was the trace of Islam, that is, its humility, its guidance, its asceticism and its bearing, and the traces of performing its obligations and its voluntary acts. And in the Hereafter, it is what He informed us they will be recognized by: the white blaze on the face and the white marks on the hands and feet from the trace of ablution, and the whiteness of faces from the trace of prostration.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of the sima (mark).
Mention of those who said this:
- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: He said: "Their sign, or the prayer has informed them."
* *
As for His saying ﴿That is their description in the Torah﴾:
He says: this quality which I have described to you of the followers of Muhammad ﷺ who are with him, is their description in the Torah.
* *
As for His saying ﴿And their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot﴾:
He says: their description in the Gospel of 'Isa is the description of a seed which produces its shoot (shat'ahu), which is its sprouts. It is said of it: the crop has sprouted (ash'ata al-zar'u) when it puts forth shoots, so it sprouts (yushti'u) ishta'. They were likened to the sprouting crop because they began to enter Islam while they were a small number, and then they kept increasing, and a group entered after them, then another group after that group, until their number grew, just as in the root of the crop a shoot comes forth, then another shoot after it, until it multiplies and grows.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.
Mention of those who said this:
- 'Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to us, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him﴾, his companions, their likeness, meaning their description written in the Torah and the Gospel before the heavens and the earth were created.
- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: 'Ubayd related to us, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers﴾ ... until His saying ﴿That is their description in the Torah﴾, then He said ﴿And their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot﴾ ... the verse.
- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, the same: ﴿That is their description in the Torah﴾: that is, this description is in the Torah. ﴿And their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot﴾: this is the description of the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Gospel.
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾, he said: ﴿That is their description in the Torah, and their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot﴾.
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration, that is their description in the Torah﴾: meaning the mark on the faces is their description in the Torah, and it is not their description in the Gospel. Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot﴾ ... the verse; this is their description in the Gospel.
- Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration, that is their description in the Torah, and their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot﴾.
- 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid related to me, he said: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him﴾ ... the verse; he said: "This is their description in the Torah, and another likeness in the Gospel: ﴿like a seed which produces its shoot, and strengthens it﴾ ... the verse."

Others said: these two likenesses are their description in the Torah and the Gospel.
Mention of those who said this:
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿That is their description in the Torah﴾: and the Gospel is the same.

The most correct of the two sayings, in our view, is the saying of the one who said: their likeness in the Torah is other than their likeness in the Gospel, and that the report about their likeness in the Torah ends at His saying ﴿That is their description in the Torah﴾. This is because if the matter were as Mujahid said, that their likeness in the Torah and the Gospel is one, the revelation would have been: "and their likeness in the Gospel, and like a seed which produces its shoot," so that the comparison with the seed would be conjoined to His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾, so that it would be a report that this is their likeness in the Torah and the Gospel. The absence of the conjunction "and" before His saying ﴿like a seed﴾ is clear evidence for the correctness of what we have said, and that the words ﴿And their description in the Gospel﴾ are a new statement about their quality which is in the Gospel, apart from what is in the Torah.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding His saying ﴿produces its shoot﴾.
Mention of those who said this:
- Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi related to me, he said: my father related to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Khaythamah, he said: While 'Abd Allah was teaching a man at sunset, he passed by this verse ﴿like a seed which produces its shoot﴾, and he said: "You are the crop, and your harvest has drawn near."
- He said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to us, he said: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Humayd al-Tawil, he said: Anas ibn Malik recited ﴿like a seed which produces its shoot, and strengthens it﴾, and said: "Do you know what its shoot is?" He said: "Its growth."
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿That is their description in the Torah, and their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot﴾: He said: "Its spike when its growth separates from its grain."
- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot﴾: He said: "This is the likeness of the companions of Muhammad ﷺ in the Gospel. It was said to them: a people will come forth who will grow like the growth of the crop, among them people who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong."
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah and al-Zuhri, regarding ﴿like a seed which produces its shoot﴾: both said: "It brought forth its growth."
- It was related to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿And their description in the Gospel is like a seed which produces its shoot﴾: meaning: the companions of Muhammad ﷺ, who will be few, then they will increase, multiply and grow strong.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 48, verse 28–29 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿like a seed that sends out its shoot﴾: "Its offspring; then its offspring multiplied."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿like a seed that sends out its shoot﴾: He said: "That which comes out beside the furrow, and it is completed and grows."

* *

As for His words ﴿so it strengthens it﴾:
It means: it strengthens it, i.e., the shoot strengthens the seed and helps it. It is from al-muwazarah (المؤازرة), which means mutual assistance (المعاونة). ﴿Then it becomes thick﴾ means: the seed becomes thick. ﴿So it stands firm upon its stalk﴾. Al-suwq (السوق) is the plural of saq (ساق), and the saq of a crop or tree is that which bears it.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.
Those who said so:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿so it strengthens it﴾: "Its growth together with its intertwining when it puts forth ears of grain." ﴿That is their likeness in the Torah, and their likeness in the Gospel﴾: It is a parable that He struck for the People of the Book: when a people emerge growing as the crop grows, and men arise among them who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and then they become strong, and they are those who were with them. It is also a parable that Allah struck for Muhammad ﷺ. He says: Allah sent the Prophet alone, then a small number gathered to him believing in him, then the few become many and grow strong, and Allah enrages the disbelievers through them.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿so it strengthens it﴾: He said: "It strengthened it and helped it."

* *

As for His words ﴿upon its stalk﴾:
He said: its roots.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah and al-Zuhri, regarding ﴿so it strengthens it, so it becomes thick, so it stands firm upon its stalk﴾: He says: "It joins together."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿so it strengthens it﴾: "It gathered together and became intertwined." He said: Likewise the believers went out while they were few and weak, and Allah continued to increase them and support them with Islam, just as He supported this seed with its offspring, so it strengthened it, and it became a parable for the believers.

⁕ Amr ibn Abd al-Hamid narrated to me, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿like a seed that sends out its shoot, so it strengthens it, so it becomes thick, so it stands firm upon its stalk﴾: He says: "A grain of wheat scattered and dispersed, so each grain sprouts one stalk, then each one of them sprouts, until it becomes thick and stands firm upon its stalk." He said: He says: The companions of Muhammad ﷺ were few, then they increased, then they became strong. ﴿That He may enrage﴾ Allah ﴿by them the disbelievers﴾.

* *

As for His words ﴿it pleases the sowers, that He may enrage by them the disbelievers﴾:
The Exalted, may His remembrance be praised, says: This crop that became thick and stood firm upon its stalk pleases those who sowed it with its completeness, its fine growth, and its reaching maturity and completion. ﴿That He may enrage by them the disbelievers﴾: He says: Likewise is the likeness of Muhammad ﷺ and his companions, and the gathering of their number until they increased and grew, and their affair became strong, like this crop whose description the Majestic One, may His praise be exalted, has described. Then He said ﴿that He may enrage by them the disbelievers﴾, which indicates an omitted part of the speech, namely that Allah did this with Muhammad ﷺ and his companions in order to enrage the disbelievers through them.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.
Those who said so:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿that He may enrage by them the disbelievers﴾: Allah says: Their likeness is like the likeness of a seed that sent out its shoot, so it strengthened it, so it became thick, so it stood firm upon its stalk, until it reached the finest growth, pleasing the sowers by its abundance and fine growth.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿it pleases the sowers﴾: "It pleases the sowers with its beauty." ﴿That He may enrage by them the disbelievers﴾: "By the believers, because of their multiplication. So this is their likeness in the Gospel."

* *

As for His words ﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them forgiveness and a great reward﴾:
The Exalted, may His remembrance be praised, says: Allah has promised those who affirmed Allah and His Messenger ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾, meaning: they acted upon what Allah commanded them of His obligations which He made binding upon them.

* *

As for His words ﴿among them﴾:
It means: from among the shoot which the seed sent out, namely those who entered Islam after the seed which our Lord, blessed and exalted is He, described. The pronoun "them" (هم) in His words ﴿among them﴾ refers to the meaning of the shoot, not its wording, and therefore it is stated in the plural "minhum" and not "minhu." The shoot is mentioned in the plural because what is intended is those who enter the religion of Muhammad ﷺ until the Day of Resurrection, after the group whose description Allah gave in His words ﴿and those with him are severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves; you see them bowing and prostrating﴾.

* *

As for His words ﴿and forgiveness﴾:
It means: pardon for what has passed of their sins and their evil deeds, by replacing them with good.

* *

As for His words ﴿and a great reward﴾:
It means: and an abundant reward, and that is Paradise.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Fath.
